=== <!-- Do NOT add Vietnam until a reliable source verifies a particular release date. Omdia is not a sufficient source; they are PROJECTING that Disney will release in Vietnam at some point. See talk page. -->Launch as a standalone Disney+ ===
Disney+ was launched early in the Netherlands on September 12, 2019, as a free trial. It officially launched in the Netherlands, United States and Canada on November 12, 2019, just before 3:00&nbsp;a.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]] ([[UTC–5]]). Disney+ launched in Australia, New Zealand and Puerto Rico on November 19, 2019, and launched in Austria, the United Kingdom, Spain, Italy, Germany, Ireland and Switzerland on March 24, 2020.<ref name="DisneyPlusLaunch" /><ref name="cnet">{{cite web |last1=Solsman |first1=Joan E. |last2=Sorrentino |first2=Mike |date=December 11, 2020 |title=Disney Plus: Everything to know about Disney's streaming app |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/disney-plus-new-hulu-bundle-movies-free-trial-verizon-espn-plus-cost/ |access-date=December 16, 2020 |publisher=[[CNET]] |archive-date=December 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201217165011/https://www.cnet.com/news/disney-plus-new-hulu-bundle-movies-free-trial-verizon-espn-plus-cost/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In the UK and Ireland, Disney+ replaced DisneyLife. In Spain, a linear Disney+ television channel launched alongside the streaming service. The channel is available exclusively on [[Movistar Plus+]], which serves as Disney+'s launch partner in the region.<ref name="Movistar">{{cite press release |title=Movistar will be the strategic distributor for Disney+ launch in Spain |date=March 8, 2020 |publisher={{lang|es|[[Telefónica]]|italic=no}} |location=Madrid |url=https://www.telefonica.com/en/web/press-office/-/movistar-will-be-the-strategic-distributor-for-disney-launch-in-spain |access-date=December 16, 2020 |author=<!-- Staff writer(s); no by-line. --> |archive-date=October 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025044243/https://www.telefonica.com/en/web/press-office/-/movistar-will-be-the-strategic-distributor-for-disney-launch-in-spain |url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2019, it was announced that [[Canal+ S.A.|Canal+]] would be the exclusive distributor of Disney+ in France.<ref name="CanalPlus">{{cite web |last=Keslassy |first=Elsa |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Disney Plus Signs Exclusive Distribution Deal With Canal Plus in France |url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-plus-canal-plus-exclusive-distribution-deal-france-1203438190/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215225022/https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-plus-canal-plus-exclusive-distribution-deal-france-1203438190/ |archive-date=December 15, 2019 |access-date=December 16, 2019 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> The launch in France was delayed from March 24 to April 7, pursuant to a request from the French government to conserve network capacity due to the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Walt Disney Company|COVID-19 pandemic]] placing additional strain on communications networks.<ref name="FranceReport">{{cite web |last=Haring |first=Bruce |date=March 21, 2020 |title=Disney+ To Reduce Bandwidth By 25 Percent, Delays France Launch Until April 7 |url=https://deadline.com/2020/03/disney-reduces-bandwidth-delays-french-debut-1202889432/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200321191113/https://deadline.com/2020/03/disney-reduces-bandwidth-delays-french-debut-1202889432/ |archive-date=March 21, 2020 |access-date=March 21, 2020 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The streaming service, along with the Disney channels were removed from the provider on December 31, 2024, after failing to renew its distrution deal between the two.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=France's Canal Plus to stop distributing Disney content from January |url=https://www.telecompaper.com/news/frances-canal-plus-to-stop-distributing-disney-content-from-january--1518004 |url-access=registration |access-date=2024-11-06 |website=Telecompaper}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{cite web |last=Paoli-Lebailly |first=Pascale |date=2024-11-05 |title=France: Disney ending Canal+ exclusivity |url=https://advanced-television.com/2024/11/05/disney-ending-canal-exclusivity/ |access-date=2024-11-06 |website=advanced-television.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In April 2020, it was announced that Disney+ original content would be licensed to pay TV and streaming operator [[OSN]], starting on April 9, in 17 countries in the [[Middle East and North Africa]] region with Disney noting that they had no current "plan to launch Disney+ as a standalone service in the region in the near future".<ref>{{cite web |last=Dams |first=Tim |date=April 2, 2020 |title=Disney Plus Originals to Play on OSN in Middle East |url=https://variety.com/2020/digital/global/disney-plus-osn-middle-east-1234569350/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200408003804/https://variety.com/2020/digital/global/disney-plus-osn-middle-east-1234569350/ |archive-date=April 8, 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2020 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=April 2, 2020 |title=Disney+ ready for Mena launch on April 9 |work=[[Gulf Daily News]] |url=http://www.gdnonline.com/Details/788742 |url-status=live |access-date=April 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200403043600/http://www.gdnonline.com/Details/788742 |archive-date=April 3, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Cornwell |first=Alexander |date=April 1, 2020 |title=Disney+ Content to Make Exclusive Middle East Debut on OSN |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-walt-disney-mideast-osn/disney-content-to-make-exclusive-middle-east-debut-on-osn-idUSKBN21K0ER |url-status=live |access-date=August 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806101724/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-walt-disney-mideast-osn/disney-content-to-make-exclusive-middle-east-debut-on-osn-idUSKBN21K0ER |archive-date=August 6, 2020}}</ref>

The service launched in Japan on June 11, 2020, as part of Disney's existing partnership with [[NTT Docomo]], and succeeded the existing [[Disney Deluxe]] service in the region.<ref name="JapanLaunch">{{cite web |last=Grater |first=Tom |date=May 28, 2020 |title=Disney+ To Launch In Japan June 11 |url=https://deadline.com/2020/05/disney-launch-japan-june-11-1202945194/|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529052306/https://deadline.com/2020/05/disney-launch-japan-june-11-1202945194/ |archive-date=May 29, 2020 |access-date=May 28, 2020 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

Few months later, Disney+ service expanded in Portugal, Belgium, Finland, Iceland, Luxembourg, Norway, Sweden and Denmark<ref>{{cite press release |title=Disney+ Continues International Expansion|date=September 15, 2020 |publisher=The Walt Disney Company Europe, Middle East & Africa |url=https://thewaltdisneycompany.eu/disney-continues-international-expansion/ |author=<!-- Staff writer(s); no by-line. --> |access-date=October 27, 2020 |archive-date=December 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230132246/https://thewaltdisneycompany.eu/disney-continues-international-expansion/ |url-status=live }}</ref> on September 15, 2020;<ref name="PortugalLaunch">{{cite news |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |author-link=Naman Ramachandran |date=June 23, 2020 |title=Disney Plus Reveals European Expansion, Pricing Plans |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |url=https://variety.com/2020/digital/news/disney-plus-europe-expansion-1234646059/ |url-status=live |access-date=June 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200624023516/https://variety.com/2020/digital/news/disney-plus-europe-expansion-1234646059/ |archive-date=June 24, 2020}}</ref> and in Latin America and the Caribbean on November 17, 2020.<ref name="LatinAmericaLaunch">{{Cite tweet |number=1295727181361012736 |user=disneyplusla |title=[NO PUBLICAR] Posteo anunciando el lanzamiento de Disney+ en Latinoamérica el 17 de noviembre. *Nota: usar hashtag #DisneyPlus |author=Disney+ Latinoamérica |date=August 18, 2020 |access-date=August 18, 2020 |language=es}}</ref>

The service expanded to Singapore on February 23, 2021.<ref name="CNA">{{cite news |last=Loh |first=Genevieve Sarah |date=December 11, 2020 |title=Mandalorian, WandaVision and more: Disney+ to launch in Singapore next year |work=[[CNA (TV network)|CNA]] |url=https://cnalifestyle.channelnewsasia.com/trending/disney-plus-singapore-launch-february-2021-13724500 |access-date=December 11, 2020 |archive-date=December 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201211010938/https://cnalifestyle.channelnewsasia.com/trending/disney-plus-singapore-launch-february-2021-13724500 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ST">{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Jan |date=December 11, 2020 |title=Disney+ streaming service launches in Singapore on Feb 23 |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/life/entertainment/disney-launching-in-singapore-on-feb-23 |access-date=June 18, 2021 |website=The Straits Times |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624202150/https://www.straitstimes.com/life/entertainment/disney-launching-in-singapore-on-feb-23 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 12, 2021, Disney announced that it would launch in the Middle East and Africa in mid-2022.<ref name="116Million">{{cite web |last=Haring |first=Bruce |date=August 12, 2021 |title=Disney Plus Tops Expectations, Reaches 116 Million Subscribers |url=https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/disney-plus-tops-expectations-reaches-116-million-subscribers-1235040516/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812200929/https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/disney-plus-tops-expectations-reaches-116-million-subscribers-1235040516/ |archive-date=August 12, 2021 |access-date=August 12, 2021 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Palmer |first=Roger |date=August 12, 2021 |title=DISNEY'S CEO BOB CHAPEK PROVIDES UPDATED DISNEY+ INTERNATIONAL ROLL OUT PLANS |url=https://whatsondisneyplus.com/disneys-ceo-bob-chapek-provides-updated-disney-international-roll-out-plans/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812205211/https://whatsondisneyplus.com/disneys-ceo-bob-chapek-provides-updated-disney-international-roll-out-plans/|archive-date=August 12, 2021 |access-date=August 12, 2021 |website=What's On Disney Plus}}</ref> Following the announcement, all the Disney+ original content has been removed from [[OSN]], which its platform were previously host Disney+ original content through licensing since April 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lakhpatwala |first=Zaira |date=March 15, 2022 |title=OSN rebrands streaming service to OSN+ |work=[[Arab News]] |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/2043171/amp|access-date=March 17, 2022 |archive-date=March 17, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220317053816/https://www.arabnews.com/node/2043171/amp |url-status=live}}</ref>

It was announced that the service would also expand to Central and Eastern Europe, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Israel, South Africa and Turkey later in between 2021 and 2022.<ref name="EESKHKLaunch">{{cite tweet |number=1337153230824943617 |user=disney |title=Across @DisneyPlus, Hotstar, Hulu, and ESPN+, Disney Direct-to-Consumer services have over 137 million subscriptions. In 2021, @DisneyPlus will launch in more markets including Eastern Europe, South Korea, Hong Kong, and more! |author=Disney |author-link=The Walt Disney Company |date=December 11, 2020 |access-date=December 16, 2020}}</ref> Among them, it has been confirmed that the service would launch on November 12, 2021, in South Korea and Taiwan, and on November 16, 2021, in Hong Kong.<ref name="DisneyPlusDay">{{cite press release |title=The Walt Disney Company Celebrates Disney+ Day on November 12 to Thank Subscribers with New Content, Fan Experiences, and More |date=September 21, 2021 |publisher=[[The Walt Disney Company]] |url=https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/the-walt-disney-company-celebrates-disney-day-on-november-12-to-thank-subscribers-with-new-content-fan-experiences-and-more/ |access-date=September 21, 2021 |author=<!-- Not stated --> |archive-date=September 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921192556/https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/the-walt-disney-company-celebrates-disney-day-on-november-12-to-thank-subscribers-with-new-content-fan-experiences-and-more/ |url-status=live}}</ref> It became available in more than 50 countries in 2022. It was going to be available in more than 160 countries by the end of 2023, but it wasn't released in more countries during that year.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 10, 2021 |title=Disney+ to Launch in 50 New Countries by Fiscal 2023 &#124; What's on Disney Plus |url=https://whatsondisneyplus.com/disney-to-launch-in-50-new-countries-by-fiscal-2023/ |access-date=November 11, 2021 |archive-date=January 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131183105/https://whatsondisneyplus.com/disney-to-launch-in-50-new-countries-by-fiscal-2023/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=November 10, 2021 |title=Disney+ Subscriber Growth Slows, Company Misses Wall Street Expectations |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/disney-q4-2021-earnings-1235045766/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=November 11, 2021 |archive-date=November 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111171134/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/disney-q4-2021-earnings-1235045766/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 29, 2022, Disney announced that it would launch the service in South Africa on May 18, 2022, in the Middle East and North Africa (excluding Syria) on June 8, 2022, in most of the remaining European countries on June 14, 2022, and in Israel on June 16, 2022.<ref name="Summer2022Launches" />

The service was also launched in the Philippines on November 17, 2022, in addition to mobile plan launch.<ref name="PH" />

=== The Disney Bundle ===
Alongside the launch of the standalone Disney+ service in the U.S., Disney also announced a [[product bundling|bundle]] including its other U.S. streaming services [[Hulu]] (ad-supported version) and [[ESPN+]], marketed as '''The Disney Bundle''', initially for [[US$]]12.99 per month;<ref name="BundleAnnouncement" /> the monthly price of this plan subsequently increased to $13.99. Additional variants of the bundle were later added including the ad-free and Live TV variants of Hulu; then, in late 2021, Disney+ and ESPN+ became non-removable parts of the Hulu + Live TV package.<ref>{{cite web |last=Perez |first=Sarah |date=November 19, 2021 |title=Hulu + Live TV is adding Disney+ and ESPN+ to its service for an additional $5 per month |url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/11/19/hulu-live-tv-is-adding-disney-and-espn-to-its-service-for-an-additional-5-per-month/ |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=[[TechCrunch]] |archive-date=August 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811141655/https://techcrunch.com/2021/11/19/hulu-live-tv-is-adding-disney-and-espn-to-its-service-for-an-additional-5-per-month/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In connection with the August 10, 2022, announcement of the ad-supported version of Disney+ launching on December 8, several new bundle options and increased prices were announced as taking effect the same day. Monthly prices for these plans range from $9.99 (for Disney Bundle Duo Basic, a new bundle with ad-supported versions of Disney+ and Hulu, but not ESPN+) to $82.99 (for Hulu + Live TV with the ad-free versions of Disney+ and Hulu streaming content, as well as ESPN+, which is only offered as an ad-supported service).<ref name="dh-disney-ads-launch">{{cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=August 10, 2022 |title=Disney+ With Ads Sets U.S. Launch Date & Pricing, Fee Hike For Premium Service; New Streaming Bundles With Hulu, ESPN+ Unveiled |url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/disneyplus-disney-advertising-tierhulu-espnplus-espn-1235089168/ |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=August 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810234308/https://deadline.com/2022/08/disneyplus-disney-advertising-tierhulu-espnplus-espn-1235089168/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The monthly price of the original bundle with ad-free Disney+, ad-supported Hulu and ESPN+ increased to $14.99; however, that plan only remains available to existing subscribers.<ref name="dh-disney-ads-launch" />

=== Launch as Disney+ Hotstar ===
{{Main|Disney+ Hotstar}}
In February 2020, Iger announced that it planned to launch Disney+ in India on March 29, 2020, by means of its existing service Hotstar, rebranding its paid tiers as a co-branded service. Hotstar was acquired by Disney during the Fox purchase, and has been the dominant streaming service in the country.<ref>{{cite web |last=Frater |first=Patrick |date=February 5, 2020 |title=Disney Plus To Launch on India's Hotstar |url=https://variety.com/2020/digital/asia/disney-plus-to-launch-india-hotstar-1203493375/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205131254/https://variety.com/2020/digital/asia/disney-plus-to-launch-india-hotstar-1203493375/ |archive-date=February 5, 2020 |access-date=February 5, 2020 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Disney+ to launch in India through Hotstar on March 29 |work=[[TechCrunch]] |url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/02/04/disney-to-launch-in-india-through-hotstar-on-march-29/ |url-status=live |access-date=February 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225213251/https://techcrunch.com/2020/02/04/disney-to-launch-in-india-through-hotstar-on-march-29/ |archive-date=February 25, 2020}}</ref> However, it was postponed due to the [[Indian Premier League]] being rescheduled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name="DisneyPlusPostponed" /> It was then launched on April 3, 2020.<ref name="DisneyPlusIndia" /> A few months later, Disney+ launched in Indonesia through Hotstar on September 5, 2020.<ref name="IndonesiaLaunch">{{cite web |last=Frater |first=Patrick |date=August 5, 2020 |title=Disney Plus Hotstar to Launch in Indonesia in September |url=https://variety.com/2020/streaming/asia/disney-plus-hotstar-indonesia-1234725872/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805182743/https://variety.com/2020/streaming/asia/disney-plus-hotstar-indonesia-1234725872/ |archive-date=August 5, 2020 |access-date=August 5, 2020 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

The Disney+ service officially launched in the 17 MENA markets, including Israel, in June 2022. Although not branded as Hotstar, a variant of the Disney+ Hotstar app for non-PC devices was made available for these markets. === Star content hub launch ===
{{Main|Star (Disney+)}}
[[Star (Disney+)|Star]], Disney's brand for non-family-oriented entertainment, launched on February 23, 2021, in Canada, Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore.<ref>{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Julia |date=December 10, 2020 |title=Disney unveils Star, its Hulu replacement for international Disney Plus subscribers |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/10/22165950/disney-star-streaming-service-hotstar-international-movies-tv |access-date=December 11, 2020 |website=[[The Verge]] |archive-date=December 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201210231742/https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/10/22165950/disney-star-streaming-service-hotstar-international-movies-tv |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=White |first=Peter |date=December 10, 2020 |title=Disney To Launch General Entertainment Streaming Service Star Globally In February |url=https://deadline.com/2020/12/disney-star-international-launch-streaming-service-1234653438/ |access-date=December 11, 2020 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=January 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128170516/https://deadline.com/2020/12/disney-star-international-launch-streaming-service-1234653438/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Star was added to Disney+ in Japan on October 27, 2021, and launched along with the service in South Korea and Taiwan on November 12 and Hong Kong on November 16 that year.<ref name="JapanSouthKorea">{{cite web |last=Frater |first=Patrick |date=September 7, 2021 |title=Disney Plus Sets Dates for Korea Launch, Japan Upgrade |url=https://variety.com/2021/global/asia/disney-plus-korea-japan-1235058494/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210908052813/https://variety.com/2021/global/asia/disney-plus-korea-japan-1235058494/ |archive-date=September 8, 2021 |access-date=September 7, 2021 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> Star was later introduced in South Africa, MENA and Eastern Europe in the summer of 2022. Disney+ in Turkey and Greece weren't carrying the Star brand due to local channels having the name, it was called "More Entertainment", instead.{{Citation needed|date=January 2023|reason=The fact that Disney+ didn't carry Star in Greece and Turkey as a result.}} It became available in the Philippines since November 17, 2022.<ref name="PH" />

The launch of Star marked the first time content classified more mature than the PG-13 and TV-14 ratings was able to be streamed on Disney+.<ref>{{cite web |last=Keeley |first=Joe |date=August 4, 2022 |title=You Can Now Watch R-Rated Movies on Disney+ in the US |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/disney-plus-r-rated-movies/ |access-date=May 4, 2023 |website=MUO |language=en}}</ref>

On May 3, 2023, the Star hub was launched in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, where [[Disney+ Hotstar]] streaming platform was available.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 5, 2023 |title=Star Brand Added to Disney+ Hotstar In Malaysia, Indonesia & Thailand |url=https://whatsondisneyplus.com/star-brand-added-to-disney-hotstar-in-malaysia-indonesia-thailand/ |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=What's On Disney Plus |language=en-us |archive-date=May 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514222629/https://whatsondisneyplus.com/star-brand-added-to-disney-hotstar-in-malaysia-indonesia-thailand/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Star was added in Latin America on June 26, 2024, replacing a separate streaming service [[Star+]], which was discontinued on July 24, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 29, 2023 |title=(Star+: )GEO Availability |url=https://help.starplus.com/geo-availability |access-date=November 29, 2023 |website=Star Plus: Help |archive-date=December 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202170326/https://help.starplus.com/geo-availability |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="StarLatAm" /><ref name="EndofStarPlus">{{cite web |url=https://alemdatela.com/fim-do-star-e-fusao-com-disney-acontecera-em-duas-etapas-entenda/ |title=Fim do Star+ e fusão com Disney+ acontecerá em duas etapas. Entenda. |trans-title=End of Star+ and merger with Disney+ begins in two steps. Know more |work=Além da Tela |date=April 19, 2024 |access-date=April 19, 2024 |language=pt}}</ref>

=== Hulu on Disney+ launch and phase-out of Star===
On December 6, 2023, Disney added a Hulu content hub to Disney+ as a beta for U.S. Disney Bundle subscribers.<ref name="HWRP"/> Disney+ only subscribers also have a small portion of Hulu catalogue available to watch. On March 27, 2024, the Hulu content hub officially exited beta.<ref name="The Verge" />

On August 6, 2025, after the completion of its acquisition of Comcast's stake in the service, Disney announced plans to fully migrate Hulu to the Disney+ platform in the United States. While Disney+ and Hulu will remain separate subscription products, their separate apps are to be replaced by a new "unified" platform in 2026. Concurrently, Disney also announced that it would replace Star with Hulu as its "global general entertainment brand" on October 8.<ref>{{cite web |last=Whittock |first=Jesse |date=August 8, 2025 |title=Hulu To Become International Tile On Disney+, Replacing Star |url=https://deadline.com/2025/08/hulu-to-become-international-tile-on-disney-replacing-star-1236479835/ |access-date=August 6, 2025 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=August 6, 2025 |title=Hulu App to Be Phased Out as Disney Is 'Fully Integrating' Service Into Disney+ |url=https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/hulu-app-phased-out-disney-plus-fully-integrating-1236480450/ |access-date=August 6, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="D+Hulu">{{cite web |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=2025-10-02 |title=Disney+ Gets Homepage Refresh As Hulu Expands Globally |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/disney-plus-homepage-refresh-hulu-expansion-1236391770/ |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="D+Hulu launch">{{cite web |last=Moss |date=2025-10-02 |title=Hulu Becomes Global General Entertainment Brand on Disney+ on Oct. 8 |url=https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/hulu-global-brand-disney-plus/ |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=The Walt Disney Company |language=en-US}}</ref>

Frank Pallotta of [[CNN]] stated that "the company [Disney] has repackaged its trove of beloved content for the service makes it a worthy companion to the other services in the marketplace.<ref>{{cite web |last=Frank Pallotta |date=12 November 2019 |title=Disney+ review: It's a lot like Netflix, but with a few twists |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/12/media/disney-plus-review/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112160125/https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/12/media/disney-plus-review/index.html |archive-date=November 12, 2019 |access-date=November 12, 2019 |publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref> Nick Pino of ''[[TechRadar]]'' stated, "If Disney keeps it updated with new content, Disney+ could rival Netflix sooner rather than later."<ref>{{cite web |last=Nick Pino |date=November 12, 2019 |title=Disney Plus review |url=https://www.techradar.com/reviews/disney-plus-review |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191113024303/https://www.techradar.com/reviews/disney-plus-review |archive-date=November 13, 2019 |access-date=November 12, 2019 |website=[[TechRadar]]}}</ref>

Upon launch, Disney+ experienced significant technical difficulties. Users complained about receiving error messages that the service was down and that they were "unable to connect", which were irritating because many of them had paid for the service months in advance.<ref>{{cite web |last=Callie Ahlgrim |date=November 12, 2019 |title=Disney Plus is already crashing on its launch day, and fans are annoyed after they paid months in advance |url=https://www.insider.com/disney-plus-crashing-technical-issues-fan-reactions-2019-11 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191201210608/https://www.insider.com/disney-plus-crashing-technical-issues-fan-reactions-2019-11 |archive-date=December 1, 2019 |access-date=November 12, 2019 |website=[[Insider (website)|Insider]]}}</ref> In some instances, passwords needed to be reset to enable access.

One other negative aspect with the launch of the service was the presentation of the non-HD episodes of ''The Simpsons''. Namely, that instead of presenting them in their original aspect ratio, they were either cropped to fit [[16:9]] widescreen televisions or awkwardly stretched out to that aspect ratio.<ref {{Short description|HTTP-based adaptive bitrate streaming technique}}

'''Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP''' ('''DASH'''), also known as '''MPEG-DASH''', is an [[adaptive bitrate streaming]] technique that enables high quality [[streaming media|streaming]] of media content over the Internet delivered from conventional [[HTTP]] web servers.

Similar to Apple's [[HTTP Live Streaming]] (HLS) solution, MPEG-DASH works by breaking the content into a sequence of small segments, which are served over [[HTTP]]. Each segment contains a short interval of playback time of content that is potentially many hours in duration, such as a movie or the live broadcast of a sport event. The content is made available at a variety of different bit rates, i.e., alternative segments encoded at different bit rates covering aligned short intervals of playback time. While the content is being played back by an MPEG-DASH client, the client uses a bit rate adaptation (ABR) algorithm<ref name="DASH-ABRLOGIC">{{cite web | url=https://github.com/Dash-Industry-Forum/dash.js/wiki/ABR-Logic| title= ABR Logic| website= [[GitHub]]}}</ref> to automatically select the segment with the highest bit rate possible that can be downloaded in time for playback without causing stalls or re-buffering events in the playback.<ref name="DASH-DYNAMIC">{{cite web | url=https://people.cs.umass.edu/~ramesh/Site/PUBLICATIONS_files/abr-dashjs.pdf| title= From Theory to Practice: Improving Bitrate Adaptation in the DASH Reference Player, by Spiteri, Sitaraman and Sparacio, ACM Multimedia Systems Conference, June 2018.}}</ref> Thus, an MPEG-DASH client can seamlessly adapt to changing network conditions and provide high quality playback with few stalls or re-buffering events.

MPEG-DASH is the first adaptive bit-rate HTTP-based streaming solution that is an international standard.<ref name="MPEGPressRelease">{{cite news |title=MPEG ratifies its draft standard for DASH |publisher=MPEG |url=http://mpeg.chiariglione.org/meetings/geneva11-1/geneva_press.htm |date=2011-12-02 |access-date=2012-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120820233136/http://mpeg.chiariglione.org/meetings/geneva11-1/geneva_press.htm |archive-date=2012-08-20 }}</ref> MPEG-DASH should not be confused with a transport protocol — the transport protocol that MPEG-DASH uses depends on which version of HTTP is used: [[Transmission Control Protocol|TCP]] is the transport over which HTTP and [[HTTP/2]] run, while [[HTTP/3]] runs over [[QUIC]] (which in turn runs over [[User Datagram Protocol|UDP]]). MPEG-DASH uses existing HTTP web server infrastructure that is used for delivery of essentially all World Wide Web content. It allows devices like Internet-connected televisions, TV set-top boxes, desktop computers, smartphones, tablets, etc. to receive multimedia content (video, TV, radio, etc.) delivered via the Internet, coping with variable Internet receiving conditions. Standardizing an adaptive streaming solution is meant to provide confidence to the market that the solution can be adopted for universal deployment, compared to similar but more proprietary solutions like [[Smooth Streaming]] by Microsoft, or [[HTTP Dynamic Streaming|HDS]] by Adobe. Unlike HDS, or Smooth Streaming, DASH is [[Agnostic (data)|codec-agnostic]], which means it can use content encoded with any [[video coding format|coding format]], such as [[High Efficiency Video Coding|H.265]], [[H.264/MPEG-4 AVC|H.264]], [[VP9]], etc.<ref name="vs">{{cite web|title=MPEG-DASH vs. Apple HLS vs. Microsoft Smooth Streaming vs. Adobe HDS|url=https://bitmovin.com/mpeg-dash-vs-apple-hls-vs-microsoft-smooth-streaming-vs-adobe-hds/|access-date=3 June 2016|date=2015-03-29}}</ref>

== Standardization ==
MPEG-DASH technology was developed under [[MPEG]]. Work on DASH started in 2010; it became a Draft International Standard in January 2011, and an International Standard in November 2011.<ref name="MPEGPressRelease" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iso.org/standard/57623.html|title=ISO/IEC 23009-1:2012|website=ISO}}</ref> The MPEG-DASH standard was published in April, 2012 but has been revised in 2019 and then once more in 2022 as [https://www.iso.org/obp/ui#iso:std:iso-iec:23009:-1:ed-5:v1:en].

DASH is a technology related to [[Adobe Systems]] [[Adaptive bitrate streaming#Adobe HTTP Dynamic Streaming|HTTP Dynamic Streaming]], [[Apple Inc.]] [[HTTP Live Streaming]] (HLS) and [[Microsoft]] [[Smooth Streaming#Microsoft Smooth Streaming|Smooth Streaming]]. DASH is based on Adaptive HTTP streaming (AHS) in [[3GPP]] Release 9 and on HTTP Adaptive Streaming (HAS) in [[Open IPTV Forum]] Release 2.<ref name="3GPP">ETSI 3GPP [http://www.3gpp.org/ftp/Specs/html-info/26247.htm 3GPP TS 26.247; Transparent end-to-end packet-switched streaming service (PSS); Progressive Download and Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (3GP-DASH)]</ref><ref>[http://www.oipf.tv/live/oipf/release_2.html Open IPTV Forum Solution Specification Volume 2a – HTTP Adaptive Streaming V2.1] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111009063030/http://www.oipf.tv/live/oipf/release_2.html |date=2011-10-09 }}</ref> As part of their collaboration with MPEG, 3GPP Release 10 has adopted DASH (with specific codecs and operating modes) for use over wireless networks.<ref name="3GPP" />

The DASH Industry Forum ([[DASH-IF]])<ref name="dashif">{{Cite web|url=https://dashif.org/|title=DASH Industry Forum &#124; Catalyzing the adoption of MPEG-DASH|website=dashif.org}}</ref> further promotes and catalyzes the adoption of MPEG-DASH and helps transition it from a specification into a real business. It consists of major streaming and media companies, including Microsoft, Netflix, Google, Ericsson, Samsung, Adobe, etc. and creates guidelines on the usage of DASH for different use cases in practice.

MPEG-DASH is integrated in other standards, e.g. MPEG-DASH is supported in [[Hybrid Broadcast Broadband TV|HbbTV]] (as of Version 1.5).<ref name="hbbtv">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hbbtv.org/pages/about_hbbtv/HbbTV-specification-1-5.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703212343/http://www.hbbtv.org/pages/about_hbbtv/HbbTV-specification-1-5.pdf|title=HbbTV Specification 1.5|archive-date=July 3, 2014}}</ref>

== Overview ==
DASH is an [[adaptive bitrate streaming]] technology where a [[multimedia]] file is partitioned into one or more segments and delivered to a client using [[HTTP]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mpeg.chiariglione.org/technologies/mpeg-b/mpb-dash/index.htm|title=Technologies &#124; MPEG|website=mpeg.chiariglione.org}}</ref> A media presentation description (MPD) describes segment information (timing, [[URL]], media characteristics like [[video|video resolution]] and [[bit rate]]s), and can be organized in different ways such as SegmentList, SegmentTemplate, SegmentBase and SegmentTimeline, depending on the use case. Segments can contain any media data, however the specification provides specific guidance and formats for use with two types of containers: [[ISO base media file format]] (e.g. MP4 file format) or [[MPEG transport stream|MPEG-2 Transport Stream]].

An early predecessor of DASH was an HTTP [[web server]] based streaming system called SProxy, developed and deployed in the Hewlett Packard Laboratories in 2006.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Chen |first1=Songqing |last2=Shen |first2=Bo |last3=Tan |first3=Wai-tian |last4=Wee |first4=Susie |last5=Zhang |first5=Xiaodong |title=2006 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo |chapter=A Case for Internet Streaming via Web Servers |date=2006-07-09 |pages=2145–2148 |doi=10.1109/ICME.2006.262660 |isbn=1-4244-0367-7 |issn=1945-7871 |eissn=1945-788X |s2cid=9202042 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Songqing |last2=Shen |first2=Bo |last3=Wee |first3=Susie |last4=Zhang |first4=Xiaodong |date=2007-07-23 |title=SProxy: A Caching Infrastructure to Support Internet Streaming |journal=IEEE Transactions on Multimedia |volume=9 |issue=5 |pages=1062–1072 |doi=10.1109/TMM.2007.898943 |bibcode=2007ITMm....9.1062C |s2cid=870854 |issn=1520-9210}}</ref> It showed how to use HTTP range requests to break the content into small segments. SProxy showed the effectiveness of segment based streaming, gaining Internet penetration in the presence of the wide deployment of firewalls (which are prone to blocking novel protocols), and reducing the unnecessary traffic transmission if a user chooses to terminate the streaming session earlier before reaching the end.

DASH is audio/video [[codec]] agnostic. One or more representations (i.e., versions at different resolutions or bit rates) of multimedia files are typically available, and selection can be made based on [[Computer Network|network]] conditions, device capabilities and user preferences, enabling [[adaptive bitrate streaming]]<ref>[http://www.mmsys.org/?q=node/43#mmt1 3GPP Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP – Standards and Design Principles] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805222811/http://www.mmsys.org/?q=node%2F43#mmt1 |date=2016-08-05 }} by T. Stockhammer</ref> and [[Fairness measure#QoE fairness|QoE (Quality of Experience) fairness]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&citation_for_view=ZDbuOE4AAAAJ:hqOjcs7Dif8C|title=Towards Network-wide QoE Fairness using OpenFlow-assisted Adaptive Video Streaming|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> DASH standard does not specify the adaptive bitrate streaming (ABR) logic.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=A Survey on Bitrate Adaptation Schemes for Streaming Media Over HTTP|first1=Abdelhak|last1=Bentaleb|first2=Bayan|last2=Taani|first3=Ali C.|last3=Begen|first4=Christian|last4=Timmerer|first5=Roger|last5=Zimmermann|date=January 21, 2019|journal=IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials|volume=21|issue=1|pages=562–585|doi=10.1109/COMST.2018.2862938|s2cid=67867085 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The current MPEG-DASH reference client dash.js<ref>{{Cite web|title=dash.js JavaScript Reference Client Landing Page|url=https://reference.dashif.org/dash.js/|access-date=2020-08-28|website=reference.dashif.org}}</ref> offers both buffer-based (BOLA<ref name="BOLA">{{cite journal | title= BOLA: Near-optimal bitrate adaptation for online videos.|arxiv = 1601.06748|last1 = Spiteri|first1 = Kevin|last2 = Urgaonkar|first2 = Rahul|last3 = Sitaraman|first3 = Ramesh K.|year = 2020|volume=28|pages=1698–1711|doi = 10.1109/TNET.2020.2996964|s2cid = 219792107|journal=IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking| issue=4 | bibcode=2020ITNet..28.1698S }}</ref>) and hybrid (DYNAMIC<ref name="DASH-DYNAMIC"/>) bit rate adaptation algorithms. DASH is also agnostic to the underlying application layer protocol. Thus, DASH can be used with other application protocols besides HTTP, e.g., DASH over [[Content centric networking|CCN]].<ref name="dashccn">{{Cite web|url=https://dash.itec.aau.at/dash-over-ccn/|title=DASH over ICN/CCN &#124; ITEC – Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP}}</ref>

On July 27, 2015, [[MPEG LA]] announced a call for MPEG-DASH-related patents in order to create a single patent pool for this technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mpegla.com/Lists/MPEG%20LA%20News%20List/Attachments/96/n-15-07-27.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150807012726/http://www.mpegla.com/Lists/MPEG%20LA%20News%20List/Attachments/96/n-15-07-27.pdf|title=MPEG LA Announces Call for Patents to Organize Joint License for MPEG-DASH|archive-date=August 7, 2015}}</ref> MPEG LA  announced its MPEG-DASH patent portfolio licence. MPEG-LA claims that the included patents are essential to the MPEG Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP standard.<ref>{{cite web |title=DASH Patent Portfolio License Briefing* |url=http://www.mpegla.com/main/programs/MPEG-DASH/Documents/DASHWeb.pdf |website=[[MPEG LA]] |date=2019-03-04 |access-date=10 July 2019}}</ref>

== Implementations ==
{{Importance section|date=August 2016}}
MPEG-DASH is available natively on Android through the ExoPlayer,<ref>{{cite web |title=ExoPlayer |url=https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/media/exoplayer |website=Android Developers |access-date=7 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> on Samsung Smart TVs 2012+, LG Smart TV 2012+, Sony TV 2012+, Philips NetTV 4.1+, Panasonic Viera 2013+ and Chromecast.<ref name="device-compatibility">[http://www.bitcodin.com/blog/2015/03/mpeg-dash-device-compatibility Device Compatibility]</ref> YouTube as well as Netflix already support MPEG-DASH, and different MPEG-DASH players are available.<ref>[http://www.dash-player.com/blog/2015/02/the-status-of-mpeg-dash-today-and-why-youtube-and-netflix-use-it-in-html5/ The Status of MPEG-DASH today, and why Youtube & Netflix use it in HTML5]</ref>

While MPEG-DASH isn't directly supported in HTML5, there are JavaScript implementations of MPEG-DASH which allow using MPEG-DASH in web browsers using the HTML5 [[Media Source Extensions]] (MSE).<ref name="mse">[https://dvcs.w3.org/hg/html-media/raw-file/tip/media-source/media-source.html HTML5 Media Source Extensions ]</ref> There are also JavaScript implementations such as the bitdash player<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bitmovin.com/video-player/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703200443/http://www.dash-player.com/demo/drm-and-protection/|title=Video Player SDKs for flawless viewing &#124; HTML5 Player|archive-date=July 3, 2015|website=bitmovin.com}}</ref> which support [[digital rights management|DRM]] for MPEG-DASH using the HTML5 [[Encrypted Media Extensions]].<ref name="eme">{{Cite web|url=https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/|title=Encrypted Media Extensions|website=w3c.github.io}}</ref> In combination with WebGL, the HTML5-based adaptive bitrate streaming of MPEG-DASH enables also the efficient streaming of 360° video for live and on-demand use cases.<ref name="360° Streaming in HTML5">{{Cite web|url=https://bitmovin.com/demos/vr-360|title=This demo shows the Bitmovin Player displaying a 360° video with VR|website=bitmovin.com |date=10 October 2023 }}</ref>

* [[VLC media player]] 3.0 shipped a new client plugin for MP4/MPEG and Live streams.<ref name="itec-dash">[http://www-itec.uni-klu.ac.at/dash/ DASH at ITEC, VLC Plugin, DASHEncoder and Dataset] by C. Mueller, S. Lederer, C. Timmerer</ref><ref name="vlc-dash-paper">{{Cite web|url=http://www-itec.uni-klu.ac.at/bib/files/p723-muller.pdf|title=C. Müller and C. * [[bitmovin]] provides the bitdash MPEG-DASH player for HTML5 and Flash.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bitmovin.com/video-player/|title=Video Player SDKs for flawless viewing &#124; HTML5 Player|website=bitmovin.com}}</ref>
* VideoJS is an open-source HTML5 video player, supports HLS, DASH, WebM, and progressive MP4 for Live and VOD streaming.<ref name="ottverse">{{cite web |last1=Vijayanagar |first1=Krishna Rao |title=Top 13 HTML5 Video Players for the Web Reviewed [2021] |url=https://ottverse.com/best-html5-video-players-for-the-web-free-and-paid/ |website=OTTVerse |date=3 June 2021 |access-date=7 December 2021}}</ref><ref name="npmtrends"/>

* [[Helix Universal Server]] has support for DASH in various modes.
*[[Nimble Streamer]] has live and VOD MPEG-DASH support. For VOD it supports both H.265 and H.264 codecs<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wmspanel.com/nimble/dash|title=MPEG-DASH streaming via Nimble Streamer - Softvelum|website=wmspanel.com}}</ref>

=== Content generators ===
* ITEC's DASHEncoder.<ref name="itec-dash" /><ref name="dataset">{{Cite web|url=http://www-itec.uni-klu.ac.at/bib/files/p89-lederer.pdf|title=S. Lederer, C. Mueller and C. Timmerer, "Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP Dataset", In Proceedings of the ACM Multimedia Systems Conference 2012, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, February 22-24, 2012.}}</ref>
* [[MP4Box]] and its multimedia framework from [[GPAC Project on Advanced Content|GPAC]] at [[Télécom Paris]]<ref name="GPAC Telecom ParisTech">{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/gpac/gpac|title=Fragmentation, segmentation, splitting and interleaving · gpac/gpac Wiki|website=GitHub}}</ref>
* dashcast from [[Télécom Paris]] supports MPEG-DASH live streaming<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gpac.wp.imt.fr/dashcast/|title=DashCast &#124; GPAC}}</ref>
* MediaGoom MPEG-DASH Packager<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mediagoom.com/|title=Media Goom. Essential Adaptive Web Streaming with MPEG-DASH and HLS|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118224209/http://mediagoom.com/|archive-date=2017-01-18}}</ref>
* Bento4 opensource tools and SDK<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bento4.com/developers/dash/|title=Getting Started - Bento4|website=www.bento4.com}}</ref>

=== Other ===
* ITEC offers a validation service for MPEG-DASH Media Presentation Description (MPD) files<ref name="itec-dash" />
* Multiple DASH datasets<ref name="MPEG DASH Dataset Overview">[http://www.dash-player.com/blog/2015/04/10-free-public-mpeg-dash-teststreams-and-datasets/ MPEG DASH Dataset Overview]</ref> are offered by the Institute of Information Technology (ITEC) at Alpen-Adria University Klagenfurt,<ref name="dataset" /><ref name="distributeddataset">{{Cite web|url=https://dash.itec.aau.at/distributed-dash-datset/|title=Distributed DASH Datset &#124; ITEC – Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP}}</ref> the GPAC group at Telecom ParisTech<ref name="GPAC Telecom ParisTech" /> and Digital TV Labs.<ref name="DASH Digital TV Labs">{{Cite web |url=http://digitaltv-labs.com/products/consumer_electronics/details/m-peg_dash |title=MPEG DASH Test Suite |access-date=2013-11-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307212517/http://digitaltv-labs.com/products/consumer_electronics/details/m-peg_dash |archive-date=2014-03-07 }}</ref>
* The BBC has DASH test streams, including DASH over HTTP/2.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/rd/blog/2013-09-mpeg-dash-test-streams|title=MPEG DASH Test Streams|website=BBC R&D|date=9 September 2013 }}</ref>
*[[Widevine]] DRM supports DASH and [[Encrypted Media Extensions]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.encoding.com/widevine/ |title=The Complete Guide to Widevine |publisher=encoding.com |access-date=2018-01-11 |archive-date=2021-12-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229023059/https://www.encoding.com/widevine/ }}</ref>
*Mividi provides software tool for analyzing and monitoring live MPEG-DASH streams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mividi.com/en-US/solutions/MPEG-DASHAnalysisandMonitoringSolution.aspx|title=MPEG-DASH Analysis and Monitoring Solution|website=mividi.com|access-date=2019-09-15}}</ref>

=== Clients ===
[[Windows 10]] used to have native support for DASH streaming in [[EdgeHTML]], a proprietary browser engine that was used in Microsoft Edge (now referred to as Edge Legacy) before the transition to the Chromium-based [[Blink (browser engine)|Blink]] browser engine. Edge Legacy was included in Windows 10 up till version 2004. It was replaced by Edge Chromium in version 20H2.

DASH support on other browsers & operating systems is available via [[Media Source Extensions]].

'''HBO Max''' (formerly known as just '''Max''' from 2023 to 2025 in select territories) is an American [[subscription video on-demand]] [[Over-the-top media service|over-the-top]] [[streaming television]] service operated by [[Home Box Office, Inc.]] on behalf of [[Skydance]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Maddaus |first=Gene |date=February 24, 2023 |title='South Park' Lawsuit: Warner Bros. Discovery Sues Paramount Global Over Licensing Dispute |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/south-park-lawsuit-hbo-max-sues-paramount-1235534780/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225003854/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/south-park-lawsuit-hbo-max-sues-paramount-1235534780/ |archive-date=February 25, 2023 |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=Variety |publisher=Variety Media |language=en-US}}</ref> The platform offers content from the [[List of libraries owned by Warner Bros. Discovery|libraries]] of [[Warner Bros. Entertainment|Warner Bros.]], [[Discovery Channel]], [[HBO]], [[CNN]], [[Cartoon Network]], [[Adult Swim]], [[Animal Planet]], [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS]], [[TNT (American TV network)|TNT]], [[TruTV]], [[Eurosport]], and their related brands. HBO Max first launched in the United States on May 27, 2020. HBO Max is the [[List of streaming media services|fifth most-subscribed video on demand]] [[streaming media]] service, after [[Disney+]], [[JioHotstar]], [[Amazon Prime Video]], and [[Netflix]], with more than 140 million paid memberships worldwide.<ref name="user2">{{cite news |title=Warner Bros Discovery Posts Strong Max Subscriber Growth In Q4, Forecasts 150M Subs By 2026-End |url=https://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/consumer/entertainment/warner-bros-discovery-forecasts-150m-subscribers-by-end-of-2026 |archive-date=February 27, 2025 |access-date=February 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250227144721/https://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/consumer/entertainment/warner-bros-discovery-forecasts-150m-subscribers-by-end-of-2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The service also carries first-run original programming under the "[[Max Originals]]" banner, programming from the HBO [[pay television]] service, and content acquired via either third-party library deals (such as those with film studios for pay television rights) or co-production agreements (including, among others, those with [[BBC Studios]] and [[Sesame Workshop]]). When the service was first launched as HBO Max, it succeeded both [[HBO Now]], a previous HBO SVOD service; and [[HBO Go]], the [[TV Everywhere]] streaming platform for HBO pay television subscribers. In the United States, HBO Now subscribers and HBO pay television subscribers were migrated to HBO Max at no additional charge, subject to availability and device support. HBO Max also supplanted the streaming component of [[DC Entertainment]]'s [[DC Universe (streaming service)|DC Universe]] service, with its original series being migrated to HBO Max as Max Originals. The HBO Max service began to expand into international markets in 2021.

According to [[AT&T]],{{efn|At the time, AT&T was the owner of HBO's then-parent company WarnerMedia.}} HBO and HBO Max had a combined total of 69.4&nbsp;million paying subscribers globally on June 30, 2021<!-- end-of-quarter data released July 22 -->, including 43.5&nbsp;million HBO Max subscribers in the U.S., 3.5&nbsp;million HBO-only U.S. subscribers (primarily commercial customers like hotels), and 20.5&nbsp;million subscribers to either HBO Max or HBO by itself in other countries.<ref name="att-2021-q2-trends">{{cite web |title=AT&T 2nd Quarter Earnings 2021 – Financial and Operational Trends |url=https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2021/q221/2Q21_Trending_Schedule.pdf#page=11 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722120320/https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2021/q221/2Q21_Trending_Schedule.pdf |archive-date=July 22, 2021 |quote=Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) Operating Volumes and Statistics (volumes in thousands) [as of 6/30/21] — HBO Max – Wholesale [Domestic]: 31,451; HBO Max – Retail [Domestic]: 12,077; International HBO Max and HBO Subscribers: 20,498}}</ref> By the end of 2021, HBO and HBO Max had a combined total of 73.8 million paying global subscribers.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=January 5, 2022 |title=HBO Max And HBO Hit 73.8M Global Subscribers At End Of 2021, Topping Company Forecasts – Update |url=https://deadline.com/2022/01/hbo-max-streaming-att-million-subscribers-2021-1234904685/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105180912/https://deadline.com/2022/01/hbo-max-streaming-att-million-subscribers-2021-1234904685/ |archive-date=January 5, 2022 |access-date=January 5, 2022 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 5, 2022 |title=HBO Max & HBO Reach 73.8 Million Subscribers Globally |url=https://www.cordcuttersnews.com/hbo-max-hbo-reach-73-8-million-subscribers-globally/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105180914/https://www.cordcuttersnews.com/hbo-max-hbo-reach-73-8-million-subscribers-globally/ |archive-date=January 5, 2022 |access-date=January 5, 2022 |website=Cord Cutters News |language=en-US}}</ref> At the end of Q1 2022, HBO and HBO Max had 76.8&nbsp;million global subscribers.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 21, 2022 |title=HBO Max and HBO Reach 76.8 Million Global Subscribers |url=https://www.cordcuttersnews.com/hbo-max-and-hbo-reach-76-8-million-global-subscribers/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220421131242/https://www.cordcuttersnews.com/hbo-max-and-hbo-reach-76-8-million-global-subscribers/ |archive-date=April 21, 2022 |access-date=April 21, 2022 |website=Cord Cutters News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Following the April 2022 merger of [[WarnerMedia]] with [[Discovery, Inc.]] to form WBD, HBO Max was one of the combined company's two flagship streaming services, the other being [[Discovery+]] (which primarily focuses on [[Factual television|factual]] and [[Reality television|reality]] programming from the Discovery brands). WBD initially announced plans for HBO Max and Discovery+ to merge in 2023, but the company ultimately chose to retain Discovery+. As part of the decision, WBD migrated some Discovery+ shows to Max while also leaving them on Discovery+. WBD went on to replace HBO Max with a newly rebranded service, shortening the service's name to "Max", which launched in the United States on May 23, 2023, in Latin America and Caribbean on February 27, 2024, and in Europe on May 21, 2024, introducing a redesigned user interface, and adding more Discovery content. The rebrand was also applied to Netherlands, Poland, France, and several other regions in 2024. In Belgium and the Netherlands, the name "HBO Max" was retained with a new Max logo. On May 14, 2025, it was announced that the "HBO Max" branding would return in the US, reverting to its original name on July 9, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adalian |first=Josef |date=2025-05-14 |title=Max Is Changing Its Name to (Get This!) HBO Max |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/hbo-max-streaming-name-change.html |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=May 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514143224/https://www.vulture.com/article/hbo-max-streaming-name-change.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

As of May 2025, Discovery+ and HBO Max have reached a combined total of 122.3 million subscribers.

== History ==

=== Original HBO Max branding ===
[[File:HBO Max Logo (October 2019).svg|thumb|First logo used from October 29, 2019, to May 22, 2023, in the United States. Used outside of the United States until June 11, 2024.]]
On October 10, 2018, WarnerMedia announced that it would launch an [[Over-the-top media services|over-the-top]] [[streaming service]] in late 2019, featuring content from its entertainment brands.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Faughnder |first1=Ryan |last2=Lee |first2=Wendy |date=October 10, 2018 |title=WarnerMedia announces new streaming service to compete with Netflix and Disney |url=https://www.latimes.com/business/hollywood/la-fi-ct-att-streaming-service-20181010-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013020508/http://www.latimes.com/business/hollywood/la-fi-ct-att-streaming-service-20181010-story.html |archive-date=October 13, 2018 |access-date=October 13, 2018 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> The original plan for the service called for three tiers with a late 2019 launch.<ref name="CNN">{{cite news |last=Stelter |first=Brian |date=July 9, 2019 |title=WarnerMedia banks on HBO's brand name for new streaming service |publisher=CNN |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/07/09/media/hbo-max-warner-media/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709200942/https://www.cnn.com/2019/07/09/media/hbo-max-warner-media/ |archive-date=July 9, 2019}}</ref> [[Randall L. Stephenson]], chairman and CEO of WarnerMedia's parent, [[AT&T]] indicated in mid-May 2019 that it would use the HBO brand and would tie into cable operators as HBO cable subscribers would have access to the streaming service. A beta was expected in the fourth quarter of 2019 and a full launch in the first quarter of 2020 at the time.<ref>{{cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=May 14, 2019 |title=HBO Pay-TV Customers Will Have Access to WarnerMedia SVOD Service, AT&T Chief Says |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/hbo-pay-tv-customers-will-have-access-to-warnermedia-svod-service-att-chief-1203214315/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710012806/https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/hbo-pay-tv-customers-will-have-access-to-warnermedia-svod-service-att-chief-1203214315/ |archive-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

[[Otter Media]] was transferred in May 2019 to WarnerMedia Entertainment from [[Warner Bros. Entertainment|Warner Bros.]] to take over the streaming service as Brad Bentley, executive vice president and general manager of direct-to-consumer development, exited the post after six months. Andy Forssell transferred from being the chief operating officer of Otter to replace Bentley as executive vice president and general manager while still reporting to Otter CEO [[Tony Goncalves]], who would lead development.<ref name="vty0">{{cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=May 31, 2019 |title=WarnerMedia Reorg Gives Otter Media's Tony Goncalves Oversight of Streaming Service Development |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/warnermedia-streaming-unit-otter-media-tony-goncalves-1203230363/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710012811/https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/warnermedia-streaming-unit-otter-media-tony-goncalves-1203230363/ |archive-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

On July 9, 2019, WarnerMedia announced that the service would be known as "HBO Max" and that it would launch in spring 2020, while [[Reese Witherspoon]]'s [[Hello Sunshine (company)|Hello Sunshine]] and [[Greg Berlanti]] were signed to production deals for the service. (The "Max" moniker is shared with HBO's sister linear pay television service [[Cinemax]], which has alternately identified by its suffix name since the mid-1980s and used it prominently in its branding from 2008 to 2011.)<ref name="city">{{cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=July 9, 2019 |title='Friends' to Leave Netflix for WarnerMedia's HBO Max Streaming Service in 2020 |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/warnermedia-hbo-max-friends-exclusive-streaming-1203262335/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709173957/https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/warnermedia-hbo-max-friends-exclusive-streaming-1203262335/ |archive-date=July 9, 2019}}</ref> On October 29, 2019, it was announced that HBO Max would officially launch in May 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last=Solsman |first=Joan E. |date=October 29, 2019 |title=HBO Max will launch in May in the US |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/hbo-max-price-release-date-launch/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191029225119/https://www.cnet.com/news/hbo-max-price-release-date-launch/ |archive-date=October 29, 2019 |access-date=October 30, 2019 |publisher=CNET}}</ref>

On January 8, 2020, AT&T announced that [[Audience (TV network)|Audience]], a channel exclusive to subscribers of AT&T-owned television providers such as [[DirecTV]] with some original programming, would be sunset on May 22, eventually transitioning to a [[barker channel]] for HBO Max.<ref>{{cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=January 9, 2020 |title=AT&T Audience Network To End; Will Transition To HBO Max Preview Channel |url=https://deadline.com/2020/01/att-audience-network-to-end-will-transition-to-hbo-max-1202825243/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111062717/https://deadline.com/2020/01/att-audience-network-to-end-will-transition-to-hbo-max-1202825243/ |archive-date=January 11, 2020 |access-date=January 10, 2020 |website=Deadline |language=en}}</ref> Warner Bros. and HBO Max announced the '''Warner Max''' film label on February 5, 2020, which would produce eight to ten mid-budget movies per year for the streaming service starting in 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=February 5, 2020 |title=Warner Bros., HBO Max Set New Film Division for Streaming Service |language=en |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/warner-bros-hbo-max-set-new-film-division-for-streaming-service-1203494178/ |url-status=live |access-date=February 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205213015/https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/warner-bros-hbo-max-set-new-film-division-for-streaming-service-1203494178/ |archive-date=February 5, 2020}}</ref> On April 20, 2020, WarnerMedia announced HBO Max's launch date as May 27.<ref>{{cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=April 21, 2020 |title=HBO Max Sets Official Launch Date |language=en |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/hbo-max-launch-date-price-streaming-1234585776/ |url-status=live |access-date=April 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422153035/https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/hbo-max-launch-date-price-streaming-1234585776/ |archive-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> Later that year on October 23, it was announced that WarnerMedia decided to consolidate the Warner Max label into the Warner Bros. Pictures Group after its chairman, [[Toby Emmerich]], and his development and production team led by Courtenay Valenti of Warner Bros. Pictures, Richard Brener of New Line and Walter Hamada (who oversees DC-based films), was put to manage the company's entire film output, both theatrical and streaming releases.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 23, 2020 |title=Warner Max Restructures as WarnerMedia Consolidates Film Production |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/warner-max-shutting-down-as-warnermedia-reorganizes-film-production |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203021149/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/warner-max-shutting-down-as-warnermedia-reorganizes-film-production |archive-date=December 3, 2020 |access-date=January 29, 2021 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |date=October 23, 2020 |title=WarnerMedia Film Group Streamline: HBO Max's Jessie Henderson To Exit, While Nikki Ramey Moves To New Line & WB |url=https://deadline.com/2020/10/warnermedia-movie-exec-streamlining-jessie-henderson-exit-nikki-ramey-new-line-wb-1234602566/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220034855/https://deadline.com/2020/10/warnermedia-movie-exec-streamlining-jessie-henderson-exit-nikki-ramey-new-line-wb-1234602566/ |archive-date=February 20, 2022 |access-date=January 29, 2021 |website=Deadline}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Donnelly |first=Matt |date=October 23, 2020 |title=HBO Max Film Shake-Up: Toby Emmerich Consolidates Power, Two Executives Depart |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/hbo-max-film-shakeup-toby-emmerich-warnermedia-1234814287/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220033412/https://variety.com/2020/film/news/hbo-max-film-shakeup-toby-emmerich-warnermedia-1234814287/ |archive-date=February 20, 2022 |access-date=January 29, 2021 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Warner Bros. Discovery era ===
In July 2022, as a part of a cost-cutting and strategic move following the merger of [[Discovery, Inc.]] with WarnerMedia to form [[Warner Bros. Discovery]] (WBD), it was reported that HBO Max had ceased new original series development in [[Central Europe]], [[Nordic countries]], the [[Netherlands]], and [[Turkey]], as well as removed selected international series from the platform worldwide. It was reported that France and Spain had been largely excluded from these cuts, due to French regulations requiring streaming services to produce domestic content, and Spanish-language content appealing to a wide range of markets served by HBO Max.<ref name="halt">{{cite web |last=Ravindran |first=Manori |date=July 4, 2022 |title=HBO Max Halts Originals in Parts of Europe in Major === Rebrand as Max ===
[[File:Max logo.svg|thumb|First Max logo used from April 12, 2023, to March 30, 2025.]]
On March 14, 2022, after Discovery shareholders approved its merger with WarnerMedia, Discovery CFO Gunnar Wiedenfels stated that the company planned to pursue an eventual merger of HBO Max with its own streaming service [[Discovery+]]. Wiedenfels stated that this process would most likely begin with a bundle of the two services as a short-term option, with a long-term goal to eventually merge the services into one platform.<ref>{{cite web |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=March 14, 2022 |title=HBO Max and Discovery Plus Will Be Combined Into One Platform |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/hbo-max-discovery-plus-combined-streaming-service-bundle-1235204060/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220317034833/https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/hbo-max-discovery-plus-combined-streaming-service-bundle-1235204060/ |archive-date=March 17, 2022 |access-date=March 16, 2022 |website=Variety}}</ref>

During an earnings call in August 2022, WBD head of Global Streaming and Interactive JB Perrette revealed that Discovery+ and HBO Max would merge "next Summer", with the unified service launching first in the United States, and rolled out to other markets beginning in late-2023.<ref name="Merge" /> When announcing the merged service, Zaslav did not immediately indicate whether it would continue to carry the HBO brand. He stated that HBO was one of the "great crown jewels of the company" and would "always be the beacon and the ultimate brand that stands for the best of television quality".<ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 5, 2022 |title=WBD Brass Stress Commitment To HBO Brand As They Mull Name For Combined Streaming Service |url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/hbo-brand-combined-streaming-service-name-warner-bros-discovery-1235085690/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805020803/https://deadline.com/2022/08/hbo-brand-combined-streaming-service-name-warner-bros-discovery-1235085690/ |archive-date=August 5, 2022 |access-date=August 5, 2022 |website=Deadline}}</ref> In early-December 2022, it was reported by CNBC via inside sources that multiple names were being considered—including simply "Max".<ref>{{cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=December 5, 2022 |title='Max' Could Be the Name of Merged HBO Max/Discovery+ Service |url=https://variety.com/2022/digital/news/name-of-hbo-max-discovery-plus-merged-service-1235450244/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221217095435/https://variety.com/2022/digital/news/name-of-hbo-max-discovery-plus-merged-service-1235450244/ |archive-date=December 17, 2022 |access-date=December 17, 2022 |website=Variety |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Sherman |first1=Alex |last2=Rizzo |first2=Lillian |title=Warner Bros. Discovery closes in on 'Max' as the name of its combined HBO Max-Discovery+ streaming service |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/12/05/warner-bros-discovery-max-streaming-service-name.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205154430/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/12/05/warner-bros-discovery-max-streaming-service-name.html |archive-date=December 5, 2022 |access-date=December 6, 2022 |publisher=CNBC |date=December 5, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2023, Zaslav revealed during an earnings call that WBD would officially announce the service on April 12.<ref name="DiscoveryPlusEconomics">{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |archive-date=February 23, 2023 |access-date=February 24, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> He also announced that WBD would continue operating Discovery+ in conjunction with the service rather than shut it down, stating that it was profitable, and that its subscribers were "very happy with the product offering".<ref name="DiscoveryPlusEconomics"/> One day before the scheduled announcement, ''[[The New York Times]]'' confirmed that the service would be called "Max", and that it would retain HBO Max's existing pricing and be available in multiple price tiers for six months (on December 5 its legacy ad-free tier will be removed with former users in this tier downgrading to the ads-supported tier after this date).<ref>{{cite news |last=Koblin |first=John |date=April 11, 2023 |title='Succession' and 'Dr. Pimple Popper' Together in New Warner Streaming App |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/11/business/media/max-streaming-warner-hbo.html |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=April 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411101428/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/11/business/media/max-streaming-warner-hbo.html |archive-date=April 11, 2023 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="Max4K">{{cite web |last=Welch |first=Chris |date=November 2, 2023 |title=Max is taking 4K away from its legacy ad-free subscribers |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/11/2/23943859/max-4k-hbo-max-ad-free-subscribers |access-date=November 18, 2023 |website=The Verge |language=en |archive-date=November 18, 2023 earlier that year from Max International, a [[nutritional supplement]] company,<ref name="Spangler">{{cite magazine |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=April 12, 2023 |title=HBO Max to Be Renamed 'Max' 2023}}</ref> for $1.8 million.<ref>{{cite web |last=Allemann |first=Andrew |title=HBO paid about $1.8 million for Max.com |website=Domain Name Wire |date=2023-10-27 |url=https://domainnamewire.com/2023/10/27/hbo-paid-about-1-8-million-for-max-com/ |access-date=2025-05-22}}</ref>

WBD officially unveiled Max on April 12: the new service would first launch in the United States on May 23, and in other regions throughout 2023 and 2024. While the new service maintains similar price points to HBO Max, support for [[4K resolution]] video and [[Dolby Atmos]] became exclusive to the new "Ultimate" tier, and the ad-free plan was also reduced from four concurrent streams to two.<ref name="AdFree">{{cite web |last=Harding |first=Scharon |date=November 2, 2023 |title=Max users grandfathered into $15.99 ad-free plan lose 4K, HDR next month |url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2023/11/max-users-grandfathered-into-15-99-ad-free-plan-lose-4k-hdr-next-month/ |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=Ars Technica |language=en-us |archive-date=November 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106123900/https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2023/11/max-users-grandfathered-into-15-99-ad-free-plan-lose-4k-hdr-next-month/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to all Warner Bros. Pictures releases from 2023 onward, WBD plans to have more library films and television series available on Max in 4K.<ref name="Spangler"/><ref name="Maas">{{cite web |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery Unveils 'Max': Everything Revealed at Combined HBO Max-Discovery+ Streaming Presentation |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/max-streaming-service-hbo-warner-discovery-1235579785/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424071008/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/max-streaming-service-hbo-warner-discovery-1235579785/ |archive-date=April 24, 2023 |access-date=April 24, 2023 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="AdFree" />

Perrette explained that the HBO branding had been dropped from the service's name so that it could be associated with its [[List of HBO original programming|original programming]] as a flagship brand on Max, rather than having to be associated with the entirety of its library—which included children's and family programming at odds with HBO having traditionally been associated with [[Pay television|premium]] and adult-oriented programming.<ref name="HBO Family">{{cite news |author-first1=Mark |author-last1=Robichaux |date=September 1, 1996 |title=Channel's Success Breeds Suitors, Imitators While Tim Robertson Has Helped Turn Family Values into Big Business, His Family Connections Are Impeding His Ambitious Plans |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-73151944.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130508070918/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-73151944.html |archive-date=May 8, 2013 |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |location=Norfolk, VA |newspaper=[[The Virginian-Pilot]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Peters |first=Jay |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery explains why it's dropping the HBO Max name |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/4/12/23673475/warner-bros-discovery-max-new-name-hbo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412200257/https://www.theverge.com/2023/4/12/23673475/warner-bros-discovery-max-new-name-hbo |archive-date=April 12, 2023 |access-date=April 12, 2023 |website=[[The Verge]]}}</ref> The Max logo was designed by the British agency DixonBaxi, and incorporates elements of both the HBO and Warner Bros. logos, including a center-dotted "a" resembling the center-dotted "O" from the HBO logo, and the "m" and "x" letters containing curves based on Warner Bros.' long-time shield logo. The service also changed its corporate color from purple to blue, in homage to Warner Bros.' historical use of blue-colored logos, and to reflect a value of being "premium but accessible".<ref>{{cite web |date=April 24, 2023 |title=DixonBaxi's new identity for streaming platform Max looks to the future |url=https://www.creativeboom.com/news/dixon-baxi-hbo-max/ |access-date=July 29, 2023 |website=Creative Boom |language=en}}</ref><ref name="PromotionalStops">{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Max Pulls Out Promotional Stops In Rebranding Promo Push As Warner Bros Discovery Looks To Make A 'Second First Impression' |url=https://deadline.com/2023/04/max-hbo-max-streaming-promotional-campaign-warner-bros-discovery-1235325661/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417100618/https://deadline.com/2023/04/max-hbo-max-streaming-promotional-campaign-warner-bros-discovery-1235325661/ |archive-date=April 17, 2023 |access-date=April 17, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

The rebrand was promoted with the tagline "The one to watch".<ref>{{cite web |title=Max's national brand campaign is all about (re)introductions |url=https://www.marketingbrew.com/stories/2023/04/18/max-s-national-brand-campaign-is-all-about-re-introductions |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Marketing Brew |language=en-us |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601191448/https://www.marketingbrew.com/stories/2023/04/18/max-s-national-brand-campaign-is-all-about-re-introductions |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Max's Marketing Boss Explains Using Old 'Harry Potter' Logo to Announce New Series, and Boosting Combined Platform's Family Focus |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/max-harry-potter-logo-launch-marketing-kids-content-1235583575/ |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601191446/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/max-harry-potter-logo-launch-marketing-kids-content-1235583575/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Pato Spagnoletto, chief marketing officer of Warner Bros. Discovery Streaming, identified the campaign as the largest marketing spend in company history.<ref name="PromotionalStops" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Maglio |first1=Tony |last2=Welk |first2=Brian |date=May 17, 2023 |title=Netflix's First Upfront Opened with a Dig at 'Max' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/business/netflix-competition-max-1234864679/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230519180716/https://www.indiewire.com/news/business/netflix-competition-max-1234864679/ |archive-date=May 19, 2023 |access-date=May 21, 2023 |website=IndieWire |language=en-US}}</ref> WBD's stock fell by nearly six percent after Max's announcement.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Vlessing |first=Etan |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery Stock Slides After Max Streaming Rebrand |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/warner-bros-discovery-stock-max-1235372644/ |url-status=live |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412214705/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/warner-bros-discovery-stock-max-1235372644/ |archive-date=April 12, 2023 |access-date=April 14, 2023}}</ref> Within the first 3 months of Max's rebrand, WBD lost 1.8&nbsp;million subscribers across their streaming platforms, but attributed it to an overlap of subscribers of Max and Discovery+, as well as expected churn.<ref>{{cite web |last=Roth |first=Emma |date=August 3, 2023 |title=HBO Max was renamed Max, and Warner Bros. Discovery lost 2.5 million streaming subscribers in the last 6 months while its rivals grew—and sports are partly to blame |url=https://fortune.com/2023/11/10/warner-bros-discovery-lost-subscribers-third-quarter-earnings-sports-streaming/ |access-date=November 12, 2023 |website=Fortune |language=en |archive-date=November 12, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112000314/https://fortune.com/2023/11/10/warner-bros-discovery-lost-subscribers-third-quarter-earnings-sports-streaming/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2024, WBD announced a partnership with [[Disney Streaming]] to offer a bundle of Max with [[Disney+]] and [[Hulu]] in the United States. It was launched on July 25, 2024, at a price of $16.99 per-month for ad-supported, and $29.99 per-month for ad-free.<ref>{{cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |title=Disney+, Hulu and Max Streaming Bundle Launches, Priced at Discount of Up to 38% |url=https://variety.com/2024/digital/news/disney-plus-hulu-max-bundle-price-release-date-1236084329/ |access-date=July 28, 2024 |website=Variety |language=en-us |date=July 25, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=May 8, 2024 |title=Disney and Warner Bros.
