=== Return to HBO Max branding ===
[[File:Max 2025 logo.svg|thumb|Final Max logo used from March 30, 2025, to July 9, 2025.]]
In February 2025, Max soft-launched a rebranding as part of its launch in Australia, changing its corporate colors from blue to monochrome; media outlets noted that this design (which uses silver or black-colored logos) closer-resembled the branding of HBO itself. The rebrand was launched globally on March 30, 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gruenwedel |first=Erik |date=March 30, 2025 |title=Max Bows Black-and-White Logo, Launches Service in Australia |url=https://www.mediaplaynews.com/max-bows-black-and-white-logo-launches-service-in-australia/ |access-date=April 1, 2025 |work=Media Play News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Murphy |first=J. Kim |date=March 30, 2025 |title=Max, Formerly Known as HBO Max, Launches New Black-and-White Logo and Color Palette, Evoking HBO Branding |url=https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/max-changes-logo-black-and-white-hbo-1236352161/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250330230248/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/max-changes-logo-black-and-white-hbo-1236352161/ |archive-date=March 30, 2025 |access-date=March 30, 2025 |work=Variety |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Pérez |first=Darío "Kentaro Darkdox" |date=March 30, 2025 |title=Max cambia su logo, pasando de azul a Blanco y Negro |url=https://www.alertageekchile.cl/2025/03/30/max-cambia-su-logo-pasando-de-azul-a-blanco-y-negro/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250330193401/https://www.alertageekchile.cl/2025/03/30/max-cambia-su-logo-pasando-de-azul-a-blanco-y-negro/ |archive-date=March 30, 2025 |access-date=March 30, 2025 |work=Alerta Geek |language=es}}</ref>

On May 14, 2025, during its upfronts, WBD announced plans to globally rename the service back to "HBO Max" later in the year. Zaslav explained that "the powerful growth we have seen in our global streaming service is built around the quality of our programming". CEO of HBO and Max Content Casey Bloys added that the HBO brand "clearly states our implicit promise to deliver content that is recognized as unique and, to steal a line we always said at HBO, worth paying for."<ref>{{cite web |last=Hibberd |first=James |date=2025-05-14 |title=Warners Reverses Course: Changes Max's Name Back to HBO Max |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/digital/max-name-change-hbo-max-upfronts-1236216616/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> On June 10, 2025, it was announced that HBO Max would expand its global rollout to 12 countries in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, where it would launch in July 2025.<ref name="HollywoodReporter"/> On July 8, 2025, it was reported that the rebranding back to "HBO Max" would begin to roll out on July 9, with ''Variety'' reporting that WBD executives wanted it to take effect before the announcement of the nominations for the [[77th Primetime Emmy Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/hbo-max-returns-max-name-change-1236450130/ |title=Max Will Change Back to HBO Max on Wednesday |last=Scheinder |first=Michael |website=Variety |date=July 8, 2025 |access-date=July 9, 2025}}</ref>

=== Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance ===
{{Main|Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance}}
On December 5, 2025, [[Netflix]] announced that it would acquire Warner Bros. Discovery for $72 billion. The deal would include HBO Max alongside the main HBO network, the [[Warner Bros. Entertainment|Warner Bros.]] film, game and television studios, [[DC Entertainment]]/[[DC Studios]], while excluding [[Discovery+]], [[CNN]], as well as the company's linear television networks, which would be [[Corporate spin-off|spun off]] into the Discovery Global company.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Netflix agrees blockbuster $72bn deal for Warner Bros studios |url=https://news.sky.com/story/netflix-agrees-blockbuster-72bn-deal-for-warner-bros-studios-13479683 |access-date=December 5, 2025 |website=[[Sky News]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Paramount Skydance]] (which hold several networks previously owned by Warner such as [[MTV]], [[Nickelodeon]], [[The Movie Channel]], [[VH1]] and [[Comedy Central]]; Paramount and Warner both own their respective stakes at [[The CW]] and [[Philo (company)|Philo]]) would later launch a hostile takeover bid for the entirety of WBD three days later for an enterprise value of $108.4 billion.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=December 8, 2025 |title=Paramount Launches Hostile Takeover Offer For Warner Bros. Discovery |url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/paramount-launches-hostile-takeover-bid-warner-bros-discovery-1236641640/ |access-date=December 8, 2025 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

After receiving a contractual waiver from Netflix in February 2026, WBD reopened negotiations with Paramount Skydance. On February 26, 2026, WBD's board determined that Paramount Skydance's revised $110.9 billion offer constituted a superior proposal to the existing Netflix agreement. Netflix declined to match the offer and withdrew, allowing Paramount Skydance to proceed as the winning bidder.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros-1236738005/ |title=That's All, Folks: Netflix Walks Away From Warner Bros., Refusing To Raise Offer |work=Deadline Hollywood |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260227004857/https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros-1236738005/ |archive-date=February 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=February 27, 2026 |title=Massive Merger Confirmed: Paramount And WBD Reveal Details Of $110 Billion Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/massive-merger-confirmed-paramount-and-wbd-reveal-details-1236738785/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=February 27, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

On April 23, 2026, WBD's shareholders approved the sale to Paramount Skydance.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 23, 2026 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery Stockholders Approve Transaction with Paramount Skydance |url=https://ir.wbd.com/news-and-events/financial-news/financial-news-details/2026/Warner-Bros--Discovery-Stockholders-Approve-Transaction-with-Paramount-Skydance/default.aspx |website=Warner Bros. Discovery - Investor Relations |access-date=April 23, 2026}}</ref> The pre-trial press conference would be on February 24, 2027, as the Paramount and Warner Bros. trial was scheduled to take place from March 2 to 19, 2027.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 4, 2026 |title=Judge Sets Paramount-WBD Merger Antitrust Trial For March |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-warner-bros-trial-1237016438/ |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en}}</ref>

On June 12, 2026, the sale was approved by the U.S. Department of Justice. In July 2026, California and 11 other U.S. states, as well as the Writers Guild of America, filed antitrust lawsuits to delay the consummation of the purchase, arguing that the combined company's share of box office and cable television revenue post-acquisition would give it undue leverage over film exhibitors and television providers. On September 21, 2026, Paramount announced a proposed out-of-court settlement, subject to a five-year consent decree mandating specific investments towards film production and acquisition, restrictions on its engagement with film exhibitors and television providers, and the establishment of an independent board to oversee the editorial integrity and independence of CBS News and CNN post-acquisition, among other conditions. The court delayed its approval in order to allow amicus briefs by parties opposed to the settlement, who argued that its antitrust remedies were not strong enough to address the original concerns raised in the suit; the settlement was approved on September 30, 2026, with Paramount stating that it expected to complete the acquisition by October 6, 2026. The merger closed as planned on that date.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=David |date=2026-10-06 |title=Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros. Discovery Officially Closes |url=https://deadline.com/2026/10/skydance-merger-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-1237147750/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US}}</ref>

The combined company originally planned to merge its streaming service [[Paramount+]] with HBO Max into one combined service.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sherman |first=Alex |date=March 2, 2026 |title=Paramount to combine HBO Max and Paramount+ into one streaming service after WBD merger |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/02/hbo-max-paramount-plus-streaming-services-merge.html |work=[[CNBC]] |access-date=March 3, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref> However, HBO and HBO Max Content CEO Casey Bloys, who took over the combined company's streaming division, stated on October 1, 2026 that the two services were more likely to be offered as a bundled subscription, and would remain operational as standalone streaming services while the Warner Bros. Discovery properties are integrated into the combined entity.<ref>{{cite news |last=Maglio |first=Tony |date=October 1, 2026 |title=Casey Bloys Indicates HBO Max and Paramount+ More Likely to Be Bundled Than Combined |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/casey-bloys-hbo-max-paramount-plus-bundle-1236718354/ |access-date=October 6, 2026 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

Existing HBO Max subscribers were grandfathered under their current plan features for six months; following that period, all legacy ad free customers were moved to the ad free tier (currently called standard tier). Existing ad supported were moved to the ad lite tier, now called basic with ads tier.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Max is coming in May |url=https://help.hbomax.com/US/Answer/Detail/000002200 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230428050455/https://help.hbomax.com/US/Answer/Detail/000002200 |archive-date=April 28, 2023 |access-date=April 28, 2023 |website=HBO Max Help Center |quote=Current HBO Max subscribers will keep their existing HBO Max plan features for at least 6 months after Max launches.}}</ref><ref name="Max4K"/>

== Management ==
HBO Max was formed under WarnerMedia's Entertainment division, then headed by [[Robert Greenblatt]]. [[Kevin Reilly (executive)|Kevin Reilly]], president of WarnerMedia Entertainment Networks, which includes most of the company's ad-supported entertainment channels such as [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS]], [[TNT (American TV network)|TNT]], and [[TruTV]]<!--not CNN (WM News & Sports), or CW / CN / Adult Swim (Warner Bros.)-->, was also given the role of as chief content officer of HBO Max with responsibility for HBO Max-exclusive original programming and library content. Andy Forssell was named the service's executive vice president and general manager while still reporting to [[Otter Media]] CEO [[Tony Goncalves]], who leads development.<ref name="city" /> Casey Bloys, programming president of HBO, retained oversight of the core HBO service but was not initially involved with Max-exclusive programming.

On August 7, 2020, WarnerMedia announced a significant restructuring under new president [[Jason Kilar]], which he described as "leaning into this great moment of change" towards direct-to-consumer services. As a result, Greenblatt and Reilly both left the company. WarnerMedia Entertainment was dissolved, with programming operations combined with Warner Bros. in a new Studios and Networks group under that studio's CEO Ann Sarnoff. Bloys was given complete programming oversight of HBO and HBO Max, as well as Reilly's other previous responsibilities, reporting to Sarnoff. Forssell became the head of a new HBO Max operating business unit, reporting directly to Kilar.<ref name="thr-restructure-2020">{{cite web |last1=Goldberg |first1=Lesley |last2=Jarvey |first2=Natalie |date=August 7, 2020 |title=Bob Greenblatt, Kevin Reilly Out Amid Major WarnerMedia Restructuring |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/bob-greenblatt-kevin-reilly-major-warnermedia-restructuring-1306486 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807204145/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/bob-greenblatt-kevin-reilly-major-warnermedia-restructuring-1306486 |archive-date=August 7, 2020 |access-date=August 7, 2020 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> On April 23, 2021, [[Adult Swim]] and HBO Max's adult animation development teams merged under the leadership of Suzanna Makkos.<ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=April 23, 2021 |title=Adult Swim & HBO Max Merge Animation Development Under Suzanna Makkos |url=https://deadline.com/2021/04/adult-swim-hbo-max-merge-animation-development-suzanna-makkos-1234742033/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220034751/https://deadline.com/2021/04/adult-swim-hbo-max-merge-animation-development-suzanna-makkos-1234742033/ |archive-date=February 20, 2022 |access-date=April 24, 2021 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

On August 15, 2022, HBO was reorganized by Warner Bros. Discovery, resulting in layoffs within HBO Max's non-scripted originals, live-action family originals, international originals, and casting units (HBO itself never had an in-house casting department). Makkos also began reporting to HBO's head of comedy Amy Gravitt.<ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 15, 2022 |title=HBO/HBO Max Layoffs Hit Max Reality, Acquisitions, Casting & Int'l; Scripted Operation Gets Restructured |url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/hbo-max-layoffs-reality-amy-gravitt-sarah-aubrey-reorg-acquisitions-casting-international-1235091596/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816014752/https://deadline.com/2022/08/hbo-max-layoffs-reality-amy-gravitt-sarah-aubrey-reorg-acquisitions-casting-international-1235091596/ |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |access-date=August 16, 2022 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 15, 2022 |title=Casey Bloys Addresses HBO/Max Reorg, "Extremely Painful" Layoff Decisions In Memo |url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/casey-bloys-hbo-max-reorg-painful-layoff-decisions-1235092839/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816014753/https://deadline.com/2022/08/casey-bloys-hbo-max-reorg-painful-layoff-decisions-1235092839/ |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |access-date=August 16, 2022 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Programming ==
{{Main|List of HBO Max original programming|List of HBO Max original films}}
HBO Max features first-run and library content from HBO and other Warner Bros. film and television studios and brands.<ref name="Content 01">{{cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |date=October 29, 2019 |title=HBO Max Programming: The TV & Film Titles That Will Stream On WarnerMedia's Service |url=https://deadline.com/2019/10/hbo-max-list-titles-originals-movies-tv-hbo-1202772182/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030025646/https://deadline.com/2019/10/hbo-max-list-titles-originals-movies-tv-hbo-1202772182/ |archive-date=October 30, 2019 |access-date=October 30, 2019 |website=Deadline |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Launch">{{cite web |last=Solsman |first=Joan E. |title=HBO Max finally sets its launch: May 27 |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/hbo-max-launch-date-may-27-prices-shows-movies-free-trials-promos-friends/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427000851/https://www.cnet.com/news/hbo-max-launch-date-may-27-prices-shows-movies-free-trials-promos-friends/ |archive-date=April 27, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |publisher=CNET |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Content 02">{{cite news |last=Haselton |first=Todd |date=July 9, 2019 |title=AT&T rolls out a new, super-charged streaming service with HBO shows, 'Friends' and more |publisher=CNBC |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/09/att-hbo-max-streaming-service-will-include-friends.html |url-status=live |access-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709180146/https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/09/att-hbo-max-streaming-service-will-include-friends.html |archive-date=July 9, 2019}}</ref> The service also includes films available through HBO's existing pay television rights that are sourced from [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] only.<ref name="Launch" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Whitten |first=Sarah |date=April 21, 2020 |title=Here's what will be available on HBO Max when it launches on May 27 |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/21/heres-what-will-be-available-on-hbo-max-when-it-launches-on-may-27.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426164846/https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/21/heres-what-will-be-available-on-hbo-max-when-it-launches-on-may-27.html |archive-date=April 26, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |publisher=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Shaw |first=Lucas |date=September 1, 2020 |title=Netflix and Amazon Elbow Way Into Talks on Streaming Hollywood Hits |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-01/flush-with-cash-streaming-giants-prep-mega-bids-for-hollywood-hits |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909144122/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-01/flush-with-cash-streaming-giants-prep-mega-bids-for-hollywood-hits |archive-date=September 9, 2020 |access-date=September 5, 2020 |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |quote=Universal Pictures and Sony Pictures have begun negotiating with streaming services and cable networks to license their next round of theatrical movies for home video, starting with films set to be released in 2022.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Vlessing |first=Etan |date=March 2, 2021 |title=Lionsgate, Summit Label Films Headed to Starz for Exclusive First Window |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/lionsgate-summit-label-films-headed-to-starz-for-exclusive-first-window-4141830 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426164846/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/lionsgate-summit-label-films-headed-to-starz-for-exclusive-first-window-4141830 |archive-date=April 26, 2020 |access-date=July 14, 2021 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en}}</ref>

As with HBO's other streaming platforms, [[HBO Go]] and [[HBO Now]] (but as opposed to its add-on services on [[Amazon Prime Video|Prime Video Channels]], [[YouTube Primetime Channels]] and, until its removal from that platform in 2021, [[Apple TV Channels]]), HBO Max originally did not include feeds of HBO's linear cable channels,<ref name="variety-hbo-confusion" /> nor does it include any content from [[Cinemax]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Baysinger |first=Tim |date=January 15, 2020 |title=Cinemax Abandons Original Programming, Channel Will Not Be Part of HBO Max |url=https://www.thewrap.com/cinemax-programming-wont-be-on-hbo-max-channel-to-no-longer-produce-original-content/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128031347/https://www.thewrap.com/cinemax-programming-wont-be-on-hbo-max-channel-to-no-longer-produce-original-content/ |archive-date=January 28, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2020 |website=[[TheWrap]]}}</ref> Though Cinemax shares its film content with the linear HBO channel, and therefore the majority of films in the combined library would be on both services in different windows, these films would not necessarily be available on both Max and Cinemax at the same time.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 25, 2019 |title=HBO Max OTT platform to include live NBA and MLB |url=https://www.sportspromedia.com/news/hbo-max-ott-platform-live-turner-sport-nba-mlb/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728222858/http://www.sportspromedia.com/news/hbo-max-ott-platform-live-turner-sport-nba-mlb |archive-date=July 28, 2019 |access-date=July 28, 2019 |website=SportsPro Media}}</ref>

On December 4, 2024, Max added a "Channels" tab offering live feeds of HBO and its linear multiplex channels (with the exception of HBO Family and HBO Latino). Initially available on a limited basis to U.S. subscribers of Max's Ad-Free and Ultimate Ad-Free tiers using adult profiles, the feature allows users to restart, rewind and fast-forward, and navigate between streams of the linear channel feeds directly from within the player.<ref>{{cite web |title=HBO's Cable Channels Begin Streaming on Max |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/hbo-cable-channels-streaming-max-1236077033/ |author-first1=Rick |author-last1=Porter |magazine=The Hollywood Reporter |date=December 4, 2024 |access-date=December 4, 2024 |archive-date=December 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204205203/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/hbo-cable-channels-streaming-max-1236077033/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Max Launches Live Feeds of HBO Programming in New In-App 'Channels' Feature |url=https://www.thewrap.com/max-live-feeds-hbo-programming-in-app-channels-feature/ |author-first1=Lucas |author-last1=Manfredi |website=The Wrap |date=December 4, 2024}}</ref>

=== Max Originals ===
{{further|List of HBO Max original programming|List of HBO Max original films|List of HBO Max exclusive international distribution programming}}
Original content produced would be under the banner ''Max Originals'', including series, films, and specials. Original episodic content is released weekly, eschewing the "[[binge-watching|binge]]" format made popular by [[Netflix]]. [[Kevin Reilly (executive)|Kevin Reilly]] stated this was to ensure that originals would remain in the spotlight for extended periods, by letting said shows "breathe" as opposed to "fading quickly after a binge and burn". He also noted that the weekly schedule helped to drive the success of past HBO shows like ''[[Succession (TV series)|Succession]]'' and ''[[Chernobyl (miniseries)|Chernobyl]]'' which they co-produced with [[Sky UK]], and became hits precisely due to their staying power.<ref name="Distribution">{{cite web |date=October 29, 2019 |title=HBO Max Original Shows Will Release New Episodes Weekly, Won't Drop Seasons All at Once |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/570108/hbo-max-release-model/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200301115217/https://www.slashfilm.com/hbo-max-release-model/ |archive-date=March 1, 2020 |access-date=March 1, 2020 |website=/Film}}</ref>

A slate of 31 original series were planned for its first year, with plans to expand to 50 for its next year, but production timelines may have been interrupted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Launch" /> Max also has podcasts about the films and TV series on the service.<ref>{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Julia |date=October 29, 2019 |title=Here's what HBO Max looks like |url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/10/29/20939183/hbo-max-interface-warnermedia-disney-netflix-launch-date-ui-gallery |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030033130/https://www.theverge.com/2019/10/29/20939183/hbo-max-interface-warnermedia-disney-netflix-launch-date-ui-gallery |archive-date=October 30, 2019 |access-date=October 30, 2019 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref> It also produces original podcasts exclusively for the service, with ''[[Batman: The Audio Adventures]]'' being the first.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carman |first=Ashley |date=August 4, 2021 |title=HBO Max is getting its own exclusive podcasts, starting with Batman |url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/8/4/22609212/hbo-max-podcast-exclusive-batman-audio-jeffrey-wright |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804190115/https://www.theverge.com/2021/8/4/22609212/hbo-max-podcast-exclusive-batman-audio-jeffrey-wright |archive-date=August 4, 2021 |access-date=September 9, 2021 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref>

=== Syndication ===
New [[Warner Bros. Television Studios|Warner Bros.]]-produced television series that have premiered on [[The CW]] since the [[2019–20 United States network television schedule|2019–20 season]] beginning with ''[[Batwoman (TV series)|Batwoman]]'' and ''[[Nancy Drew (2019 TV series)|Nancy Drew]]'' would have their past seasons placed on HBO Max about a month after the season finale airs on television (streaming rights to existing series remains with Netflix under an existing deal). ''[[Katy Keene (TV series)|Katy Keene]]'' left HBO Max on July 9, 2025.<ref name="city" /> Although the ''[[All American (TV series)|All American]]'' spin-off, ''[[All American: Homecoming]]'', which premiered on the CW in 2022, was placed on [[Netflix]] with its parent show. On July 9, 2019, HBO Max acquired the U.S. streaming rights to ''[[Friends]]'' in a $425&nbsp;million deal,<ref name="city" /><ref name="Launch" /> and on September 17, 2019, acquired the U.S. streaming rights to ''[[The Big Bang Theory]]'', as part of a deal that also extends TBS's off-network rights to the series through 2028.<ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=September 17, 2019 |title=HBO Max Lands 'The Big Bang Theory' Streaming Rights, TBS Extends Cable Window In Mega WarnerMedia Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2019/09/hbo-max-l-the-big-bang-theory-streaming-rights-tbs-extends-cable-window-mega-deal-warnermedia-1202736725 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190928231232/https://deadline.com/2019/09/hbo-max-l-the-big-bang-theory-streaming-rights-tbs-extends-cable-window-mega-deal-warnermedia-1202736725/ |archive-date=September 28, 2019 |access-date=October 3, 2019 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

=== Acquired rights ===
Outside of Warner Bros. Discovery, the service also offers titles from [[The Criterion Collection]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Perez |first=Sarah |date=October 30, 2019 |title=HBO Max Will Cost $14.99 Per Month and Launch in May 2020 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/29/hbo-max-will-cost-14-99-per-month-and-will-launch-in-may-2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226185314/https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/29/hbo-max-will-cost-14-99-per-month-and-will-launch-in-may-2020/ |archive-date=December 26, 2019 |access-date=December 26, 2019 |website=TechCrunch |language=en}}</ref> and has a long-term partnership with [[BBC Studios]] (which HBO had previously partnered with to create ''[[His Dark Materials (TV series)|His Dark Materials]]''). Over 700 episodes of BBC content were available on the service at launch, including the first 11 seasons of the 2005 ''[[Doctor Who]]'' revival, as well as future seasons twelve through fourteen, and a variety of other shows including ''[[The Honourable Woman]]'', ''[[Luther (TV series)|Luther]]'', ''[[Top Gear (2002 TV series)|Top Gear]]'', and the original British version of ''[[The Office (British TV series)|The Office]]''. Additionally, future shows by BBC Studios would be co-produced with HBO Max.<ref name="BBC Studios">{{cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=August 1, 2019 |title='Luther,' 'Doctor Who,' U.K. 'Office' Libraries Head to HBO Max in BBC Deal |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/luther-doctor-who-uk-office-libraries-head-hbo-max-bbc-deal-1228564 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801213448/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/luther-doctor-who-uk-office-libraries-head-hbo-max-bbc-deal-1228564 |archive-date=August 1, 2019 |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

HBO also extended their existing partnership with [[Sesame Workshop]], while moving said content to the front of the HBO Max brand. Select episodes from all fifty seasons of ''[[Sesame Street]]'' (dating back to 1969) are available to stream on the service for the first time ever.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 3, 2019 |title=HBO Max and Sesame Workshop Announce New Content Partnership Cementing a Shared Commitment to Kids and Families |url=https://www.sesameworkshop.org/press-room/press-releases/hbo-max-and-sesame-workshop-announce-new-content-partnership-cementing |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422043454/https://www.sesameworkshop.org/press-room/press-releases/hbo-max-and-sesame-workshop-announce-new-content-partnership-cementing |archive-date=April 22, 2020 |access-date=May 7, 2020 |website=Sesame Workshop}}</ref> Additionally, future seasons of ''Sesame Street'' streamed exclusively on HBO Max until 2025, alongside ''[[Esme & Roy]]'', and several new spin-offs starting with ''[[The Not-Too-Late Show with Elmo]]'', ''[[Sesame Street: Mecha Builders]]'', and ''The Monster at the End of This Story''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Julia |date=October 3, 2019 |title=HBO Max Locks Down Exclusive Access to New Sesame Street Episodes |url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/10/3/20897104/sesame-street-streaming-hbo-mwarnermedia-pbs-disney-apple-streaming-wars |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201113192856/https://www.theverge.com/2019/10/3/20897104/sesame-street-streaming-hbo-max-warnermedia-pbs-disney-apple-streaming-wars |archive-date=November 13, 2020 |access-date=May 26, 2020 |website=The Verge}}</ref> On March 8, 2022, WarnerMedia and Sesame Workshop announced they would plan new shows for Cartoon Network for the new original series run and a second run acquisition rights HBO Max, including ''[[Charlotte's Web (miniseries)|Charlotte's Web]]'', and ''[[Bea's Block]]'' as well as the animation special ''Sesame Street: The Nutcracker''. In addition, new episodes to start of the 53rd season of ''Sesame Street'' and spin-offs would be available to stream on HBO Max in selecting Asian territories while holding the second run acquisition rights to replace PBS, more than a new first run for Cartoon Network.<ref>{{cite press release |title=WarnerMedia Kids & Family and Sesame Workshop Expand Content Partnership with New Animated Adventures and Fresh Takes on Family Classics |date=March 8, 2022 |publisher=[[Sesame Workshop]] |url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2022/03/08/warnermedia-kids-and-family-and-sesame-workshop-expand-content-partnership-with-new-animated-adventures-and-fresh-takes-on-family-classics-722114/20220308warnermedia01/ |access-date=April 2, 2022 |via=The Futon Critic}}</ref>

HBO Max has acquired the streaming rights to several [[Comedy Central]] series, including ''[[South Park]]'', ''[[Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens]]'', ''[[South Side (TV series)|South Side]]'', and ''[[The Other Two]]''; with the latter two becoming Max Original series.<ref>{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 13, 2020 |title='The Other Two' & 'South Side' Move to HBO Max, Streamer Nabs 'Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens' SVOD Rights in Comedy Central Prods. Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2020/08/comedy-central-the-other-two-south-side-hbo-max-originals-awkwafina-is-nora-from-queens-svod-rights-1203012460/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200823235557/https://deadline.com/2020/08/comedy-central-the-other-two-south-side-hbo-max-originals-awkwafina-is-nora-from-queens-svod-rights-1203012460/ |archive-date=August 23, 2020 |access-date=August 24, 2020}}</ref>

In November 2021, HBO Max acquired the rights to [[TV Globo|Globo]]'s [[telenovelas]] and series for Latin America and the Caribbean outside of Brazil.<ref name="TV Globo">{{cite web |date=November 24, 2021 |title=Globo fecha acordo e HBO Max vai exibir novelas e séries da emissora |url=https://www.tvpop.com.br/31032/globo-fecha-acordo-e-hbo-max-vai-exibir-novelas-e-series-da-emissora/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124174910/https://www.tvpop.com.br/31032/globo-fecha-acordo-e-hbo-max-vai-exibir-novelas-e-series-da-emissora/ |archive-date=November 24, 2021 |access-date=November 24, 2021}}</ref>

In February 2022, [[Sony Pictures]] and WarnerMedia announced that they would extend their agreement to carry films from its subsidiary companies in its Central and Eastern Europe pay television window rights window along with the library of television series produced by its sister company [[Sony Pictures Television Studios]], the deal would also include the rights to its releases beginning in 2022 for broadcasting on its channels and would be streaming it on HBO Max throughout Central and Eastern Europe.<ref name="Sony">{{cite web |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Sony, WarnerMedia Set Blockbuster Film Deal for HBO Max Central Europe |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/sony-hbo-max-central-europe-film-deal-spider-man-ghostbusters-1235176770/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220319194806/https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/sony-hbo-max-central-europe-film-deal-spider-man-ghostbusters-1235176770/ |archive-date=March 19, 2022 |access-date=February 18, 2022 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

In June 2021, HBO Max ordered a pilot from [[John Wells (filmmaker)|John Wells]] and ''[[Animal Kingdom (TV series)|Animal Kingdom]]'' writer Matt Kester for ''Ke Nui Road,'' an action drama following a team of lifeguards in the [[North Shore (Oahu)|North Shore]] of [[O'ahu]], [[Hawaii]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Peter |date=June 28, 2021 |title=John Wells & Matt Kester's Lifeguard Drama ''Ke Nui Road'' Picked Up To Pilot At HBO Max |url=https://deadline.com/2021/06/john-wells-matt-kester-lifeguard-drama-ken-nui-road-pilot-hbo-max-1234783059 |access-date=October 18, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> HBO Max would not go forward with the series, and it would instead be given a series order by [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] as ''[[Rescue: HI-Surf]]''.<ref name="Sea Shimooka">{{cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |date=January 18, 2024 |title=Fox Sets Cast for Lifeguard Drama Series ''Rescue: Hi Surf'' |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/fox-lifeguard-drama-rescue-hi-surf-cast-1235877059/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240118231523/https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/fox-lifeguard-drama-rescue-hi-surf-cast-1235877059/ |archive-date=January 18, 2024 |access-date=January 18, 2024 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

In August 2021, [[Funimation]], a subsidiary of [[Sony]], purchased Crunchyroll from AT&T for $1.175&nbsp;billion, with the intent to create a combined service that caters to anime entertainment.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=D'Anstasio |first=Cecelia |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Welcome to the Era of Big Anime |url=https://www.wired.com/story/funimation-crunchyroll-big-anime-era-is-here/ |url-status=live |magazine=Wired |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220101193610/https://www.wired.com/story/funimation-crunchyroll-big-anime-era-is-here/ |archive-date=January 1, 2022 |access-date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> On January 1, 2022, HBO Max removed the Crunchyroll hub, instead redirecting subscribers to a "global animation" page that combines selected anime with other international animated films. Since then, the service has slowly started to remove anime from Crunchyroll's line up.<ref>{{cite web |last=Valentine |first=Evan |date=December 3, 2021 |title=HBO Max Set to Lose Crunchyroll Next Year |url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/hbo-max-drops-crunchyroll-2022/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104043005/https://comicbook.com/anime/news/hbo-max-drops-crunchyroll-2022/ |archive-date=January 4, 2022 |access-date=January 3, 2022 |website=Comic Book}}</ref>

On November 22, 2021, [[Disney]] and WarnerMedia reached a deal to amend the pre-existing contract HBO had with [[20th Century Studios]] to allow [[Disney+]] or [[Hulu]] and HBO Max to share the streaming rights to half of 20th Century Studios' and [[Searchlight Pictures]]' 2022 theatrical slate in the United States during the pay-one window, with ''[[Ron's Gone Wrong]]'' being the first film under the deal, becoming available on both Disney+ and HBO Max on December 15, 2021.<ref name="20thHBO2022">{{cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=November 22, 2021 |title=Disney, WarnerMedia Carve Up Fox Film Slate Streaming Rights Through End of 2022 (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/disney-warnermedia-fox-movies-streaming-2022-1235117329/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531221143/https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/disney-warnermedia-fox-movies-streaming-2022-1235117329/ |archive-date=May 31, 2022 |access-date=December 21, 2021 |website=Variety}}</ref> Disney would still have full streaming rights to any 20th Century Studios and Searchlight Pictures films produced for Disney+ or Hulu, while the Disney deal with WarnerMedia for streaming 20th Century Studios and Searchlight Pictures films on HBO Max ended in 2022, with Disney+ and Hulu assuming the full pay-one rights to those films in the future.

On February 15, 2022, it was announced that first-run episodes of ''South Park'' would move to [[Paramount+]] beginning with season 27 in 2024, and the series library would move from HBO Max to the service in the United States in 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hailu |first=Selome |date=February 15, 2022 |title='South Park' to Stream Exclusively on Paramount Plus After HBO Max Deal Ends |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/south-park-stream-paramount-plus-1235182902/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220509025129/https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/south-park-stream-paramount-plus-1235182902/ |archive-date=May 9, 2022 |access-date=May 9, 2022 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

Discovery+ would remain the main streaming home of its programming.<ref>{{cite web |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=August 4, 2022 |title=Magnolia Network Shows Go to HBO Max and CNN Originals Go to Discovery+ as Warner Bros. On October 7, 2022, HBO Max announced ''[[Harley Quinn (TV series)|Harley Quinn]]: A Very Problematic Valentine's Day Special'', which premiered on February 23, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mitovich |first=Matt Webb |date=October 7, 2022 |title=Harley Quinn Valentine's Special Set for February, Will Also Check In on Superman/Lois and Other Couples |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/harley-quinn-valentines-special-release-date-february-2023-1234884533/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014095608/https://tvline.com/2022/10/07/harley-quinn-valentines-special-release-date-february-2023/ |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=October 12, 2022 |website=TVLine |language=en-US}}</ref>

With the announced rebrand of HBO Max as Max, WBD announced several new projects, including a [[Wizarding World#Future television series|television series adaptation of ''Harry Potter'']] planned to premiere in the 2025–26 season and run for ten years, and ''[[It – Welcome to Derry|It: Welcome to Derry]]''—a prequel series to [[Andy Muschietti]]'s film adaptation of [[It (2017 film)|''It'']]. ==== "{{vanchor|Project Popcorn}}": Warner Bros. same-day premieres ====
In late 2020, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], WarnerMedia moved two Warner Bros. films originally intended as major theatrical releases to either exclusive or simultaneous releases on HBO Max. ''[[The Witches (2020 film)|The Witches]]'' was released exclusively on HBO Max in the U.S. on October 22,<ref>{{cite news |last=Holt |first=Kris |title='The Witches' skips theaters for an HBO Max debut on October 22nd |language=en |work=Engadget |url=https://www.engadget.com/the-witches-release-date-hbo-max-anne-hathaway-robert-zemeckis-145900255.html |url-status=live |access-date=November 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007230841/https://www.engadget.com/the-witches-release-date-hbo-max-anne-hathaway-robert-zemeckis-145900255.html |archive-date=October 7, 2020}}</ref> and ''[[Wonder Woman 1984]]'' debuted simultaneously in North American theaters and on HBO Max on December 25, although the latter was initially only available on the service for a month.<ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=November 18, 2020 |title='Wonder Woman 1984' Going In Theatres & HBO Max On Christmas Day, Unprecedented For A Superhero Tentpole |url=https://deadline.com/2020/11/wonder-woman-1984-going-in-theaters-hbo-max-on-christmas-day-1234618288/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118235549/https://deadline.com/2020/11/wonder-woman-1984-going-in-theaters-hbo-max-on-christmas-day-1234618288/ |archive-date=November 18, 2020 |access-date=November 19, 2020 |website=Deadline}}</ref> Week-long free trials were discontinued in December 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Mitchell |date=December 4, 2020 |title=Hope you weren't planning to watch Wonder Woman 1984 with an HBO Max free trial |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/4/22154553/hbo-max-ditches-one-week-free-trial-ahead-of-wonder-woman-1984 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205171840/https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/4/22154553/hbo-max-ditches-one-week-free-trial-ahead-of-wonder-woman-1984 |archive-date=December 5, 2020 |access-date=December 5, 2020 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref>

On December 3, 2020, it was announced that the studio's entire 2021 film lineup would see a simultaneous theatrical release and a one-month limited release on the streaming service, starting with ''[[The Little Things (2021 film)|The Little Things]]'' on January 29.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 30, 2021 |title=When Does 'The Little Things' Leave HBO Max? |access-date=February 17, 2021 |website=Men's Health |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Tom & Jerry (2021 American film)|Tom and Jerry]]'' (February 26), ''[[Godzilla vs. Kong]]'' (March 31), ''[[Mortal Kombat (2021 film)|Mortal Kombat]]'' (April 23), ''[[Those Who Wish Me Dead]]'' (May 14), ''[[The Conjuring: The Devil Made Me Do It]]'' (June 4), ''[[In the Heights (film)|In the Heights]]'' (June 10), ''[[Space Jam: A New Legacy]]'' (July 16), ''[[The Suicide Squad (film)|The Suicide Squad]]'' (August 5), ''[[Reminiscence (2021 film)|Reminiscence]]'' (August 20), ''[[Malignant (2021 Standard release windows applied to each film after their initial limited-run streaming release on the service; HBO Max would then reassume streaming rights to the aforementioned Warner Bros. films upon their respective pay television premieres on the linear HBO service in mid-to-late 2021 or 2022, depending on the scheduled start of their individual HBO exhibition agreements.<ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=December 3, 2020 |title=Warner Bros Sets Entire 2021 Movie Slate To Debut On HBO Max Along With Cinemas In Seismic Windows Model Shakeup |url=https://deadline.com/2020/12/warner-bros-2021-movie-slate-hbo-max-matrix-4-dune-in-the-heights-1234649760/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203194850/https://deadline.com/2020/12/warner-bros-2021-movie-slate-hbo-max-matrix-4-dune-in-the-heights-1234649760/ |archive-date=December 3, 2020 |access-date=December 14, 2020 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Whitbrook |first=James |date=December 3, 2020 |title=Every 2021 Warner Bros Film Will Stream on HBO Max for Free |url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/every-2021-warner-bros-film-will-stream-on-hbo-max-for-1845800868 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206122833/https://io9.gizmodo.com/every-2021-warner-bros-film-will-stream-on-hbo-max-for-1845800868 |archive-date=December 6, 2020 |access-date=December 7, 2020 |website=Gizmodo}}</ref>

This decision, called "Project Popcorn" within Warner Bros.,<ref name="deadline-2022">{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=January 3, 2022 |title=With Tentpoles Bound To Surge The 2022 Box Office, The Great Theatrical-Streaming Day & Date Experiment Goes Out Like A Dud In 2021 |url=https://deadline.com/2022/01/2022-box-office-theatrical-streaming-day-date-experiment-1234902774/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220103194518/https://deadline.com/2022/01/2022-box-office-theatrical-streaming-day-date-experiment-1234902774/ |archive-date=January 3, 2022 |access-date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> was met with backlash from filmmakers, production companies, the [[Directors Guild of America]], the [[Creative Artists Agency]], and movie theater owners as Warner Bros. had not informed anyone about their plan ahead of the announcement.<ref name="nolan-hbo-max">{{cite web |date=December 8, 2020 |author-first1=Kim |author-last1=Masters|title=Christopher Nolan Rips HBO Max as "Worst Streaming Service," Denounces Warner Bros.' Over HBO Max Deal |language=en-US |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/directors-guild-warner-bros-hbo-max-deal-1234849614/ |url-status=live |access-date=December 9, 2020 Warner Bros. spent over $200{{nbsp}}million alone compensating talent for the shift to streaming; ''Deadline'' reported in January 2022 that such a business move "will never occur again given its high cost".<ref name="deadline-2022" />

In March 2021, it was announced that Warner Bros. would discontinue same-day releases in 2022, as part of an agreement the studio reached with [[Cineworld]] (who operates [[Regal Cinemas]]) and would instead use a 45-day exclusive release window for theaters.<ref>{{cite web |last1=D'Alessandro |first1=Anthony |last2=Tartaglione |first2=Nancy |date=March 23, 2021 |title=Regal Cinemas To Reopen In April; Parent Cineworld & Warner Bros Reach Multi-Year Deal To Show WB Films In U.S. & UK |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/cineworld-regal-warner-bros-deal-theatrical-windows-us-cinemas-reopening-1234719255/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909212321/https://deadline.com/2021/03/cineworld-regal-warner-bros-deal-theatrical-windows-us-cinemas-reopening-1234719255/ |archive-date=September 9, 2021 |access-date=March 24, 2021 |website=Deadline |quote=Cineworld and Warner Bros. have also hatched a multi-year agreement that would see the No. 2 global exhibitor show the studio's 2021 theatrical and HBO Max day-and-date titles in the U.S. as of their theatrical release. Then, beginning in 2022, Warner Bros. theatrical films will have a 45-day window of theatrical exclusivity at Cineworld's Regal chain.}}</ref> ''[[The Matrix Resurrections]]'' was the final film released in 2021 as part of Project Popcorn. The 45-day release window for HBO Max was only used for two films (''[[The Batman (film)|The Batman]]'' and ''[[Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore]]'') before it was reported in August 2022 that, as part of a restructuring of Warner Bros.' film distribution strategy following the merger of WarnerMedia and Discovery, Inc., the length of the window would now be decided for each film on a case-by-case basis.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 5, 2022 |title=Warner Bros. Movies No Longer Moving to HBO Max After 45 Days in Theaters |url=https://collider.com/warner-bros-movies-hbo-max-45-day-release-release-window-cancelled/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805210713/https://collider.com/warner-bros-movies-hbo-max-45-day-release-release-window-cancelled/ |archive-date=August 5, 2022 |access-date=September 7, 2022 |website=Collider}}</ref>

=== CNN Max ===
{{Redirect|CNN Max|CNN's current streaming service|CNNgo|CNN's former streaming service|CNN+}}
[[File:CNN Max.svg|thumb|CNN Max logo]]
On August 13, 2023, CNN announced a new streaming news hub on Max known as '''CNN Max''' to launch on September 27, which features a mix of original news programs and simulcasts of primetime programs from CNN's U.S. and international linear networks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Steinberg |first=Brian |date=August 24, 2023 |title=Live-Streamed CNN Channel With New Shows Set to Debut on Max |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/cnn-live-streamed-news-max-1235703599/ |access-date=September 6, 2023 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=September 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907013706/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/cnn-live-streamed-news-max-1235703599/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Darcy |first=Oliver |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/24/media/cnn-max-streaming/index.html |title=CNN is launching a live service on Max with new programming as the network reboots its streaming efforts |date=August 25, 2023 |access-date=November 7, 2023 |publisher=CNN |language=en-US |archive-date=November 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107094330/https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/24/media/cnn-max-streaming/index.html |url-status=live}}</ref> [[CNN International]] is also available through Max in European countries such as France and Poland.<ref name="BeneluxNo3" />

CNN had previously attempted a standalone subscription service in 2022, [[CNN+]], but was closed almost immediately after the completion of the WarnerMedia/Discovery merger due to it conflicting with the company's goal of having one streaming service to encompass all WBD properties.<ref name="cnbc-2022-04-21">{{cite web |last=Sherman |first=Alex |date=April 21, 2022 |title=CNN+ is shutting down, effective April 30, sources say |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/04/21/cnn-is-shutting-down-effective-april-30-sources-say.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506183631/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/04/21/cnn-is-shutting-down-effective-april-30-sources-say.html |archive-date=May 6, 2022 |access-date=April 21, 2022 |publisher=CNBC}}</ref><ref name="nytimes-2022-04-21">{{cite news |last1=Grynbaum |first1=Michael |last2=Koblin |first2=John |last3=Mullin |first3=Benjamin |date=April 21, 2022 |title=CNN+ Streaming Service Is Set to Shut Down |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/21/business/cnn-plus-shutting-down.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220421155004/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/21/business/cnn-plus-shutting-down.html |archive-date=April 21, 2022 |access-date=April 21, 2022 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

On March 30, 2025, HBO Max has removed this feature on the basic with ads plan.<ref>{{cite web |last=Vlessing |first=Etan |date=2025-02-26 |title=Max Pulls CNN and Sports From Ad Tier in Streaming Pivot |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/max-sports-news-content-1236147664/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 3, 2025, HBO Max announced that CNN Max would be discontinued on November 17, 2025, with no reason given, with the development of the all access plan for CNN digital content, called '''CNN All Access''' (launched on October 28, 2025).<ref>{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2025-10-03 |title=CNN Live News Stream Being Pulled From HBO Max As Network Prepares To Launch New Streaming Channels |url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/cnn-hbo-max-streaming-news-1236569187/ |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Fischer |first=Sara |date=2025-10-28 |title=CNN launches new All Access subscription service |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/10/28/cnn-all-access-subscription-mark-thompson |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref>

=== Sports on HBO Max ===
{{Main|TNT Sports (United States)}}
On March 1, 2022, Turner Sports announced an eight-year deal to hold rights to [[United States men's national soccer team|United States men's]] and [[United States women's national soccer team|women's]] national soccer team home matches, such as FIFA World Cup qualifying and international friendlies. This excludes [[FIFA]] and [[CONCACAF]] events, whose rights are held by Fox, and away matches. It was stated that at least half the matches per-season would be exclusive to HBO Max.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 1, 2022 |title=WarnerMedia signs eight-year deal with U.S. Soccer for men's and women's national team matches |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/soccer/warner-media-us-soccer-deal-hbo-max-tnt-tbs.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302063912/https://awfulannouncing.com/soccer/warner-media-us-soccer-deal-hbo-max-tnt-tbs.html |archive-date=March 2, 2022 |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=Awful Announcing |language=en-US}}</ref> The first match was streamed on January 17, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last=Forristal |first=Lauren |date=January 17, 2023 |title=HBO Max subscribers can now livestream US national soccer games |url=https://techcrunch.com/2023/01/17/hbo-max-livestream-us-national-soccer-games/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117144516/https://techcrunch.com/2023/01/17/hbo-max-livestream-us-national-soccer-games/ |archive-date=January 17, 2023 |access-date=December 14, 2023 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 5, 2023, HBO Max announced plans to launch a new sports-focused tier in the United States, to be known initially as the '''[[Bleacher Report]] Sports add-on'''. The tier would feature live sporting events and studio shows from [[TNT Sports (United States)|TNT Sports]], including [[Major League Baseball]] ([[MLB on TBS|MLB]]), the [[National Basketball Association]] ([[NBA on TNT|NBA]]), the [[National Hockey League]] ([[NHL on TNT|NHL]]), and the [[NCAA March Madness (TV program)|NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], as well as exclusive USA Soccer matches and programs, and select on-demand content.<ref name="SportsAddOn">{{Cite web |last=Bucholtz |first=Andrew |date=2024-09-05 |title=WBD reportedly set to start charging for Max sports add-on in September |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/warner-bros-discovery/max-sports-add-on-charge.html |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Awful Announcing |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="LiveSportsTier">{{cite web |date=September 19, 2023 |title=Max will start offering a live sports tier in October |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/19/23880831/max-live-sports-tier-launch-date-price |access-date=September 19, 2023 |website=[[The Verge]] |language=en-US |archive-date=September 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230919191224/https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/19/23880831/max-live-sports-tier-launch-date-price |url-status=live}}</ref> On December 14, 2023, amid the closure of the [[Global Cycling Network|GCN+]] service, WBD announced that its programming rights would be consolidated into the sports add-on in February 2024, including the [[Giro d'Italia]] and various [[Union Cycliste Internationale|UCI]] tours and events.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 15, 2023 |title=Max To Welcome Live Cycling in the U.S. in February 2024 |url=https://www.sportsvideo.org/2023/12/15/max-to-welcome-live-cycling-in-the-us-in-february-2024/ |access-date=April 5, 2024 |website=Sports Video Group |language=en |archive-date=April 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240405003059/https://www.sportsvideo.org/2023/12/15/max-to-welcome-live-cycling-in-the-us-in-february-2024/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The service was to be available as a free preview until February 29, 2024, after which it was to become an $9.99 add-on on top of an existing Max subscription. However, amid changes to TNT Sports' portfolio (including its impending loss of rights to the NBA in 2025, and other acquisitions such as college sports and international events such as the [[French Open]]), the launch of the sports add-on as a paid service was delayed indefinitely.<ref name="SportsAddOn" /><ref name="LiveSportsTier" /> On February 26, 2025, it was announced that the add-on had been scrapped as part of a change in strategy, and that live sports content would be available at no additional charge as part of the "Standard" and "Premium" tiers of Max (as B/R sports on Max). JB Perrette stated that WBD had been "actively involved in exploring ways to evolve the sports distribution ecosystem in the U.S.", and that offering sports content as part of the existing tiers was the best option for subscribers.<ref>{{cite web |last=Steinberg |first=Brian |date=2025-02-26 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery's Max Scraps Plan to Launch Separate Sports Tier |url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/warner-bros-discovery-max-scraps-separate-sports-tier-launch-1236321101/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=February 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250226165651/https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/warner-bros-discovery-max-scraps-separate-sports-tier-launch-1236321101/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Lerner |first=Drew |date=2025-02-26 |title=Max ditches B/R Sports add-on, will include sports in Standard and Premium tiers |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/tnt-sports/max-ditches-sports-add-on-include-standard-premium-tiers.html |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Awful Announcing |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Eurosport add-on ===
Similar to the Bleacher Report Sports add-on in the United States, a sports-focused tier was added to Max in Europe during its launch over the summer of 2024 in conjunction with its pan-European sports brand [[Eurosport]]. This tier would offer the linear channels [[Eurosport 1]] and [[Eurosport 2]], and coverage for various sports events including the [[2024 Summer Olympics]], Giro d'Italia, [[Vuelta a España]], and [[Tour de France]].<ref name="BeneluxNo3" />

=== TNT Sports Premium add-on ===
On July 9, 2024, Warner Bros. Discovery announced that [[TNT Sports (Chilean TV channel)|TNT Sports]] would arrive at Max in Chile the week of July 15 with an innovative proposal where sports fans would be able to subscribe independently or by adding it to the platform's available plans. It would include live events and original content.

The most relevant Chilean soccer competitions are added, such as the [[Chilean Primera División]], [[Primera B de Chile|Primera B]], [[Copa Chile]] and original programming, among others.<ref>{{cite web |last=TNT Sports Chile |date=July 9, 2024 |title=TNT Sports llega a Max |url=https://tntsports.cl/nacional/TNT-Sports-llega-a-Max-con-lo-mejor-del-futbol-chileno-20240709-0017.html |access-date=May 14, 2025}}{{Dead link|date=June 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref>

From February 2025, [[TNT Sports (Argentine TV channel)|TNT Sports]] content would be available to users with a subscription to [[Argentine Primera División|Pack Fútbol]] with their enabled cable operator and to TNT Sports subscribers independently.

=== Max DAZN Package ===
From October 24, 2024, in Spain, Max has added a new '''Max DAZN''' package that costs €44.99 per month, in addition to the Sports package that is optional for the Standard and Premium plans, it includes four [[DAZN]] channels in addition to [[Eurosport]] with the best sport that fans could wish for.

[[La Liga]], the [[UFC]], or the [[Formula 1]] and [[Grand Prix motorcycle racing|MotoGP]] world championships would be available to subscribers of the '''Max DAZN''' Package, in addition to having all the movies, series and documentaries on the platform with the same advantages as the Premium Plan.<ref>{{cite web |last=Cazallas |first=Javier |date=2024-10-24 |title=Max deporte que nunca con la llegada de DAZN como plan de suscripción a la plataforma: LaLiga, F1, MotoGP… |url=https://www.hobbyconsolas.com/noticias/max-deporte-nunca-llegada-dazn-como-plan-suscripcion-plataforma-laliga-f1-motogp-1413951?0= |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=Hobby Consolas |language=es |archive-date=December 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241225095625/https://www.hobbyconsolas.com/noticias/max-deporte-nunca-llegada-dazn-como-plan-suscripcion-plataforma-laliga-f1-motogp-1413951?0= |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Technologies and accessibility ==
At launch, HBO Max did not support [[Ultra-high-definition television|4K]], [[High-dynamic-range video|HDR]], [[Dolby Vision]], or [[Dolby Atmos]], but support for these technologies were planned as "part of the HBO Max product roadmap".<ref>{{cite web |last=Machkovech |first=Sam |date=May 28, 2020 |title=HBO Max is live: $15/mo for a massive library, significant headaches |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2020/05/hbo-max-impressions-the-blockbuster-video-of-streaming-not-a-compliment/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529072611/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2020/05/hbo-max-impressions-the-blockbuster-video-of-streaming-not-a-compliment/ |archive-date=May 29, 2020 |access-date=May 29, 2020 |website=Ars Technica |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Heller |first=Emily |date=May 27, 2020 |title=Everything you need to know about HBO Max |url=https://www.polygon.com/2020/5/27/21266205/hbo-max-pricing-devices-launch-date-free-upgrade-shows |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200531071824/https://www.polygon.com/2020/5/27/21266205/hbo-max-pricing-devices-launch-date-free-upgrade-shows |archive-date=May 31, 2020 |access-date=May 29, 2020 |website=Polygon |language=en}}</ref> Support for 4K, HDR, and Atmos was added starting with the release of ''Wonder Woman 1984'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Excited to announce that #WW84 will be the first film on HBO Max available in 4K Ultra HD, HDR 10, Dolby Vision AND Dolby Atmos! Can't wait. IN THEATERS on Dec. 25th and exclusively streaming in the US on @hbomax. PLEASE find the biggest and highest quality screen you can!! |url=https://twitter.com/PattyJenks/status/1333861228695875584 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811054656/https://twitter.com/PattyJenks/status/1333861228695875584 |archive-date=August 11, 2022 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |via=Twitter |language=en}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=June 2024}} with WarnerMedia promising to add more content in these formats throughout 2021 and beyond.<ref>{{cite web |last=Welch |first=Chris |date=December 1, 2020 |title=Wonder Woman 1984 will be the first title that HBO Max streams in 4K |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/1/21813364/wonder-woman-1984-4k-ultra-hd-dolby-vision-atmos-announced |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217135100/https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/1/21813364/wonder-woman-1984-4k-ultra-hd-dolby-vision-atmos-announced |archive-date=February 17, 2021 |access-date=January 31, 2021 |website=The Verge |language=en |quote=This is the very start, and HBO Max will "expand these capabilities to further films and TV series, as well as adding support for additional devices, throughout 2021."}}</ref>

The service provided [[closed captioning]] support at launch, but initially lacked support for [[audio description]] (AD) for those with visual impairments.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 27, 2020 |title=Streaming Video Services Offering Audio Description |url=https://acb.org/adp/streaming.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200506141216/https://www.acb.org/adp/streaming.html |archive-date=May 6, 2020 |access-date=May 30, 2020 |website=The Audio Description Project |publisher=[[American Council of the Blind]] |quote=[U]sers report that there is no AD in this [HBO Max] App, and it is not very accessible.}}</ref> In October 2020, the [[American Council of the Blind]] announced it had reached a settlement with WarnerMedia whereby at least 1,500 hours of HBO Max content would be available with AD by the end of March 2021, increasing to at least 6,000 hours by March 2023, along with other [[accessibility]] enhancements to the website and apps by September 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last=American Council of the Blind |date=October 19, 2020 |title=Accessibility Enhancements on the Horizon for HBO Max Customers Who are Blind |url=https://acb.org/HBO-accessibility |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101025135/https://acb.org/HBO-accessibility |archive-date=November 1, 2020 |access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref> HBO Max later began rolling out AD on select titles on March 26, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 26, 2021 |title=HBO Max Rolls Out Audio Described Content |url=https://acb.org/HBO-Max-audio-description |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210329132616/https://www.acb.org/HBO-Max-audio-description |archive-date=March 29, 2021 |access-date=April 2, 2021 |publisher=[[American Council of the Blind]]}}</ref>

HBO Max also offers selected content with [[American Sign Language]] (ASL) [[Language interpretation|interpretation]]; in 2025, season 2 of ''[[The Last of Us (TV series)|The Last of Us]]'' became the first television series on a streaming service to offer a signed version of its first-run episodes.<ref>{{cite web |last=Winslow |first=George |date=2025-03-21 |title=Max To Debut 'The Last Of Us' with American Sign Language |url=https://www.tvtechnology.com/news/max-to-debut-the-last-of-us-with-american-sign-language |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=TV Tech |language=en}}</ref> In June 2025, tying in with its setting and themes, it was announced that ''[[Sinners (2025 film)|Sinners]]'' would become the first film to be offered on a streaming platform in [[Black American Sign Language]] (BASL).<ref>{{cite web |last=Maglio |first=Tony |date=2025-06-30 |title='Sinners' on Max Will Include a Black American Sign Language Version |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/sinners-black-american-sign-language-basl-version-on-max-1236302908/ |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Distribution ==

=== United States ===
The majority of active subscribers to the HBO pay TV service (which previously included HBO Go), and most customers that were subscribed to HBO Now at time of launch, can access HBO Max for no extra charge, with all three services generally sharing the same price point of $14.99 per month. However, this transition is contingent on the customer's current provider or biller having signed a new distribution agreement for HBO Max with WarnerMedia.<ref name="variety-hbo-confusion">{{cite web |last1=Spangler |first1=Todd |last2=Schneider |first2=Michael |date=October 30, 2019 |title=HBO Max vs. HBO Now vs. HBO Go: Why WarnerMedia's Strategy May Lead to Brand Confusion |url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/hbo-max-now-go-warnermedia-price-branding-1203388699/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031005101/https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/hbo-max-now-go-warnermedia-price-branding-1203388699/ |archive-date=October 31, 2019 |access-date=October 31, 2019 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref name="fiercevideo-pitch">{{cite web |last=Munson |first=Ben |date=November 20, 2019 |title=WarnerMedia chief pitches HBO Max to Comcast and other distributors |url=https://www.fiercevideo.com/cable/warnermedia-chief-pitches-hbo-max-to-comcast-and-other-distributors |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200101174325/https://www.fiercevideo.com/cable/warnermedia-chief-pitches-hbo-max-to-comcast-and-other-distributors |archive-date=January 1, 2020 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |website=FierceVideo}}</ref>

On May 27, 2020, as part of an agreement with Time Warner that renewed its carriage contract for the [[Turner Broadcasting System]] networks and gave its over-the-top television service [[Sling TV]] distribution rights to the linear HBO channel. [[Dish Network]] secured an option to become a distribution partner for HBO Max following the exclusivity period with Apple.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Joe Flint |last2=Shalini Ramachandran |date=May 27, 2020 |title=Turner and Dish Reach New Distribution Pact |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |publisher=[[News Corp (2013–present)|News Corp.]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/turner-and-dish-reach-new-distribution-pact-1427905296 |url-status=live |access-date=May 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801201621/https://www.wsj.com/articles/turner-and-dish-reach-new-distribution-pact-1427905296 |archive-date=August 1, 2020}}{{subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Chris Welch |date=May 27, 2020 |title=HBO is coming to Sling TV this month |work=The Verge |url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/4/1/8326089/hbo-coming-to-sling-tv |url-status=live |access-date=May 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801125457/https://www.theverge.com/2015/4/1/8326089/hbo-coming-to-sling-tv |archive-date=August 1, 2020}}</ref> HBO content is also available as a premium add-on for [[DirecTV Stream]] and [[Hulu]] for the same $14.99 price as HBO Max.<ref>[https://www.consumerreports.org/movies-tv/ways-to-watch-hbo/ 6 Ways to Watch HBO] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101020806/https://www.consumerreports.org/movies-tv/ways-to-watch-hbo/ |date=November 1, 2021}}. Consumer Reports.</ref>

In announcing HBO Max, WarnerMedia immediately confirmed that HBO subscribers on AT&T-owned platforms (including [[AT&T TV]], [[DirecTV]], [[U-verse]], and [[AT&T Mobility]]) would receive HBO Max on-launch at no additional charge.<ref>{{cite web |last=Katzmaier |first=David |title=Millions of HBO and HBO Now subscribers will get HBO Max for free |access-date=October 30, 2019 |publisher=CNET |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Blumenthal |first=Eli |title=AT&T plans to include HBO Max for free at launch for 10M current subscribers |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/at-t-plans-to-include-hbo-max-for-free-at-launch-for-10-million-current-subscribers/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030202259/https://www.cnet.com/news/at-t-plans-to-include-hbo-max-for-free-at-launch-for-10-million-current-subscribers/ |archive-date=October 30, 2019 |access-date=October 30, 2019 |publisher=CNET |language=en}}</ref> AT&T customers who are subscribed to their highest-tiered internet, TV and wireless plans would also receive HBO Max for free, while 2020 |publisher=CNET |language=en}}</ref> Existing HBO Now subscribers billed directly by HBO were also migrated to HBO Max on-launch at no additional charge. On April 27, 2020, an agreement was announced for HBO Now subscribers via Apple (both in-app subscriptions and [[Apple TV Channels]]) to be migrated to HBO Max. Content from HBO Max would be listed in the [[Apple TV app]] along with there being a dedicated HBO Max hub in the app.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=April 27, 2020 |title=HBO Max Sets Apple Deal For Streaming Distribution |url=https://deadline.com/2020/04/hbo-max-apple-streaming-distribution-1202918784/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427182744/https://deadline.com/2020/04/hbo-max-apple-streaming-distribution-1202918784/ |archive-date=April 27, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=Deadline |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Gartenberg |first=Chaim |date=April 27, 2020 |title=WarnerMedia expands free HBO Max deal to HBO subscribers who pay through Apple's services |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/4/27/21238601/hbo-max-apple-subscribers-free-now-in-app-purchase-tv-channel |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428071900/https://www.theverge.com/2020/4/27/21238601/hbo-max-apple-subscribers-free-now-in-app-purchase-tv-channel |archive-date=April 28, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref> On [[Apple TV (device)|Apple TV]] devices, HBO Max is available to the regular fourth generation Apple TV and fifth and sixth generation [[Apple TV 4K]]; earlier versions which do not support third-party app download are not supported.

The most prominent platforms without agreements to carry HBO Max at the launch were [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] (maker of the [[Fire TV]] and [[Fire HD]] devices) and [[Roku, Inc.|Roku]], which together are estimated to control 70% of the U.S. streaming player market.<ref name="wsj-amazon-roku-impasse" /> With both platforms, non-Max HBO content remained available as usual through the companies' respective channels platforms or through HBO Now (which was rebranded to just "HBO" on July 31, 2020) while deals for HBO Max were being worked out. impasse following the launch, reportedly due to a disagreement about whether Amazon can host the additional Max programming directly on its [[Amazon Prime Video]] Channels platform as it does for HBO currently.<ref>{{cite web |last=Littleton |first=Cynthia |date=May 13, 2020 |title=John Stankey: AT&T's SVOD and Linear TV Platforms to 'Become One' in Future
